body.text: namaḥ śrīsarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ
body.translated_text: Homage to all the blessed <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājāmātyair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍair gandharvaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātraśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme.
body.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, townsfolk, merchants, caravan leaders, <s>devas</s> (gods), <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>—thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>—the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, known as one of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines for the sick, together with the <s>Saṅgha</s> of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s> in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena śrāvastyām anāthapiṇḍado nāma gṛhapatiḥ prativasaty āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī.
body.translated_text: Now at that time in <s>Śrāvastī</s> there dwelt a householder named <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, who was wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive holdings, equaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth.

body.text: tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam. sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati. tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ patnī āpannasattvā saṃvṛttā. sāṣṭānāṃ navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā.
body.translated_text: He had taken a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported, enjoyed himself, and amused himself with her. While he was sporting, enjoying, and amusing himself, his wife became pregnant. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth.

body.text: dārikā jātā, abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetā sā unnītā vardhitā mahatī saṃvṛttā, jñātibhir asyāḥ sumāgadheti nāma vyavasthāpitam.
body.translated_text: A girl was born—beautiful, lovely, pleasing, endowed with all major and minor limbs. She was raised and nurtured and grew up. Her relatives established her name as <s>Sumāgadhā</s>.

body.text: puṇḍravardhane 'pi ca nagare mūṣilo nāma gṛhapatiḥ prativasaty āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī.
body.translated_text: In the city of <s>Puṇḍravardhana</s> also there dwelt a householder named <s>Mūṣila</s>, who was wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive holdings, equaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth.

body.text: tasya putro vṛṣabhadatto nāma, so 'py abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetaḥ, sa cānyatīrthyasaṃsargān nirgrantheṣv abhiprasanno 'bhūt.
body.translated_text: He had a son named <s>Vṛṣabhadatta</s>, who was also handsome, lovely, pleasing, endowed with all major and minor limbs. Due to his association with followers of other sects, he had become devoted to the <s>Nirgranthas</s> (Jain ascetics).

body.text: yadā bhagavatānuttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ tadā sarve 'nyatīrthyā bhagnāḥ parājitāḥ pratyantaṃ samāśritāḥ, kecit gauḍikaṃ grāmaṃ, kecit puṇḍravardhanaṃ nagaraṃ, kecit bhadrikaṃ nagaram.
body.translated_text: When the <s>Bhagavān</s> performed the miracle of supernatural powers (<s>ṛddhiprātihārya</s>) in the supreme human realm, all the other sectarians were defeated, vanquished, and took refuge in the outlying regions—some to the village of <s>Gauḍika</s>, some to the city of <s>Puṇḍravardhana</s>, some to the city of <s>Bhadrika</s>.

body.text: sa ca gṛhapatiputro dainyenāvatiṣṭhate, sa ca nirgranthair ucyate: kim arthaṃ tvaṃ no vivāhayasīti. sa provāca: patnī me sadṛśī na vidyate. ta ūcur: anāthapiṇḍadasya duhitā sumāgadhā nāmāsti, sāpi abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā janapadakalyāṇīsadṛśī, tāṃ prārthayeti.
body.translated_text: The householder's son lived in wretchedness. The <s>Nirgranthas</s> said to him: 'Why do you not marry?' He replied: 'There is no wife equal to me.' They said: '<s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> has a daughter named <s>Sumāgadhā</s>, who is also beautiful, lovely, pleasing, comparable to the beauty of the land—seek her hand.'

body.text: tato 'sau sahaśravaṇād eva tasyāṃ saṃraktacitto babhūva. yāvad anyatīrthikaveśaṃ kṛtvānupūrveṇa śrāvastīm anuprāptaḥ, piṇḍapātram anuvicarann anāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhaṃ praviṣṭaḥ. sumāgadhā bhikṣāṃ gṛhītvā nirgatā. sā tena dṛṣṭā. sahadarśanād evātīva saṃraktacitto babhūva. sa bhrāntena khorakena śaktuṃ pratigṛhnāti, mathitaṃ ca sikkāyāṃ.
body.translated_text: Then, upon merely hearing of her, his mind became enamored. Disguising himself in the garb of a non-Buddhist ascetic, he gradually reached <s>Śrāvastī</s> and, wandering for alms, entered the house of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. <s>Sumāgadhā</s> came out carrying alms food. He saw her. Upon seeing her, his mind became exceedingly enamored. With bewildered and confused [hands], he took the barley flour, and the stirred [drink] on the ladle.

body.text: tataḥ sumāgadhā tam asaṃvṛtendriyaṃ dṛṣṭvā prahasitā, āha ca: asaṃprajānā ime 'nyatīrthyā bhikṣāṃ pratigṛhṇantīti. tataḥ so 'pi tayā saha prahasito bhikṣāṃ gṛhītvā prakrāntaḥ.
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sumāgadhā</s>, seeing him with uncontrolled senses, laughed and said: 'These non-Buddhist ascetics accept alms without awareness.' Then he too, having been laughed at by her, took the alms and departed.

body.text: tataḥ puṇḍravardhanaṃ gatvā pitur niveditavān. tena sā dārikā śrāvastīṃ gatvā yācitā.
body.translated_text: Then, having gone to <s>Puṇḍravardhana</s>, he informed his father. The father went to <s>Śrāvastī</s> and asked for the girl.

body.text: anāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā bhagavān pṛsṭaḥ. bhagavān āha: gṛhapate, pravrajitām idam akaraṇīyam. api tu yadi sumāgadhā puṇḍravardhanaṃ yāsyati, tatrāpi buddhakāryaṃ kariṣyatīti.
body.translated_text: The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Householder, this is not to be done for a renunciant. However, if <s>Sumāgadhā</s> goes to <s>Puṇḍravardhana</s>, she will accomplish the work of the <s>Buddha</s> there as well.'

body.text: tato 'nāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā sumāgadhā mahatā śrisamudayena vṛṣabhadattāya dattā, tenāpi svagṛhaṃ nītā.
body.translated_text: Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> gave <s>Sumāgadhā</s> with great splendor and wealth to <s>Vṛṣabhadatta</s>, and he took her to his own home.

body.text: yāvad apareṇa samayena tasmin gṛhe nirgranthā bhuñjate, sā śvaśruṇocyate: dārike, āgaccha dakṣiṇīyān paśyeti.
body.translated_text: Now on another occasion, <s>Nirgranthas</s> were dining in that house. She was told by her mother-in-law: 'Daughter, come see the worthy recipients [of gifts].'

body.text: tasyā buddhir abhavat: nūnaṃ sthavirāryaśāradvatīputramahāmaudgalyāyanāryānandaprabhṛtayo mahāśrāvakā upanimantritā iti. sā hṛṣṭatuṣṭā nirgatā.
body.translated_text: She thought: 'Surely the great disciples such as the elder <s>Āryaśāradvatīputra</s> (<s>Śāriputra</s>), <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, <s>Āryānanda</s>, and others have been invited.' Delighted and pleased, she went out.

body.text: tayā te nirgranthāḥ kākapakṣamalinā malapaṭalavastrā durgandhaśarīrā nagnāḥ pretasadṛśā dṛṣṭvā ca punar durmanāḥ saṃvṛttā.
body.translated_text: She saw those <s>Nirgranthas</s>—filthy as crows' wings, wearing garments covered with grime, with foul-smelling bodies, naked, resembling hungry ghosts—and became dejected.

body.text: sā śvaśruṇocyate: dārike, kimarthaṃ parikhinnāsīti. sā provāca: ārye, yady evaṃvidhā dakṣinīyāḥ. pāpakārinaḥ punaḥ kīdṛśā bhavantīti.
body.translated_text: Her mother-in-law said to her: 'Daughter, why are you distressed?' She replied: 'Venerable lady, if such as these are the worthy recipients, then what must evildoers look like?'

body.text: sā kathayati: dārike, 'sti kaścid ebhyo 'nyaḥ prativiśiṣṭataraḥ śāstā loke.
body.translated_text: She [the mother-in-law] says: 'Daughter, is there anyone in the world who is a more distinguished teacher than these?'

body.text: sā kathayati: asti śrāvastyāṃ pitur me vihāre sa bhagavān upeto mātṛtaḥ pitṛtaḥ saṃśuddhaḥ, kṣatriyo jātyā, rājakulāt pravrajitaś cakravartivaṃśāt; uccāt kulāt pravrajito 'nūnāt. punar aparaṃ, sa bhagavān āḍhyāt kulāt pravrajito 'dīnāt. punar aparaṃ, sa bhagavān daharas taruṇaḥ pratyagrayauvanasamanvāgataḥ.
body.translated_text: She [<s>Sumāgadhā</s>] says: 'In <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the monastery of my father, there is that <s>Bhagavān</s>—pure on both mother's and father's side, a <s>Kṣatriya</s> by birth, gone forth from a royal family, from the lineage of a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch); gone forth from a high family, not a lowly one. Furthermore, that <s>Bhagavān</s> went forth from a wealthy family, not a poor one. Furthermore, that <s>Bhagavān</s> is young, in his youth, endowed with the freshness of early manhood.'

body.text: yasmin samaye krīḍāharṣamaṇḍanavibhūṣaṇasthānayogam anuyuktena vihartavyam, tasmin samaye 'kāmakānāṃ jñātīnām sāśrukaṇṭhānāṃ rudanmukhānāṃ keśaśmaśrūṇy avatārya kāśāyāṇi vastrāṇy ācchādya samyag eva śraddhayāgārād anagārikāṃ pravrajitaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'At that age when one should engage in the pleasures of sporting, adorning, and decorating—at that very time, against the will of his weeping and tearful-throated relatives, he shaved his hair and beard, put on the saffron robes, and with perfect faith went forth from the household life into homelessness.'

body.text: punar aparaṃ, bhagavān dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samanvāgato 'sītyanuvyañjanair virājitagātro vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaḥ, sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaḥ, jaṅgama iva ratnaparvataḥ samantato bhadrako 'bhirūpako darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, the <s>Bhagavān</s> is endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great person, his body resplendent with eighty secondary characteristics, adorned with a halo extending a full fathom, his radiance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, altogether auspicious, handsome, lovely, and pleasing.'

body.text: jñātvā sa bhagavān dṛṣṭvā, sanidānaṃ śrāvakānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati nānidānaṃ, saniḥsaraṇaṃ nāniḥsaraṇaṃ, saparikramaṃ nāparikramaṃ, sapratisaraṇaṃ nāpratisaraṇaṃ, saparākramaṃ nāparākramaṃ, saprātihāryaṃ nāprātihāryam.
body.translated_text: 'Having known and seen, that <s>Bhagavān</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to his disciples with a basis, not without a basis; with an escape, not without an escape; with a gradual path, not without a gradual path; with a refuge, not without a refuge; with a heroic effort, not without a heroic effort; with miraculous display, not without miraculous display.'

body.text: prajñāvan sa bhagavān mahāprājñaḥ, alam utpannānāṃ paravādināṃ saha dharmeṇa nirgṛhītā, alaṃ svakasya vādasya pratiṣṭhāpayitā, karmavādī sa bhagavān kriyāvādī.
body.translated_text: 'That <s>Bhagavān</s> is wise, greatly wise, fully capable of refuting the proponents of opposing doctrines by the <s>Dharma</s>, capable of establishing his own doctrine. That <s>Bhagavān</s> is a proponent of <s>karma</s> (action), a proponent of action.'

body.text: pūrvābhilāpī sa bhagavān priyabhāṣī, uttānamukhavarṇo vigatabhṛkuṭiḥ smitapūrvaṃgamaḥ. ehīti svāgatavādī, kalyāṇavākyaḥ sa bhagavān bāhyakaraṇopetaś, citrakathaḥ sa bhagavān madhurakathaḥ, kalyāṇapraṇidhāno bahuhitānukampī bahvanekajanatāvinīta.
body.translated_text: 'That <s>Bhagavān</s> speaks first, speaks pleasantly, with upturned face and clear complexion, free from frowning, with a smile preceding [his words]. He is one who says "Come, welcome." That <s>Bhagavān</s> is of auspicious speech, endowed with open-handedness; that <s>Bhagavān</s> is of varied discourse, of sweet discourse, of auspicious resolve, compassionate toward the welfare of many, the trainer of many diverse multitudes of people.'

body.text: āryadharmatayā nyāyadharmatayā virajadharmatayā atuladharmatayā labdhasahāyaḥ sa bhagavān, bahavo 'sya sahāyakāḥ śīlasaṃpannāḥ samādhisaṃpannāḥ prajñāsaṃpannā vimuktisaṃpannā vimuktijñānasaṃpannāḥ.
body.translated_text: 'That <s>Bhagavān</s> has obtained allies through the noble <s>Dharma</s>, the righteous <s>Dharma</s>, the pure <s>Dharma</s>, the incomparable <s>Dharma</s>. He has many allies who are accomplished in <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), accomplished in <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), accomplished in <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), accomplished in <s>vimukti</s> (liberation), accomplished in the knowledge of liberation.'

body.text: punar aparaṃ; sa bhagavān yaṃ grāmakṣetram upaniśritya viharati, na tatra manuṣyā amanuṣyā vā viheṭhayanti, kālena kālaṃ divyāni rūpāṇi dṛśyante, divyāḥ śabdāḥ śrūyante, udārāś cāvabhāsāḥ prajñāyante, devaḥ kālena kālaṃ samyag vāridhārām anuprayacchatīti.
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, whatever village or territory that <s>Bhagavān</s> resides in, there neither humans nor non-humans cause harm. From time to time divine forms are seen, divine sounds are heard, and great illuminations are perceived. The rain-god sends down proper rain showers at the appropriate time.'

body.text: tasyāḥ sahaśravaṇād eva bhagavato 'ntike cittam abhiprasannaṃ, sā prasannacittā kathayati: dārike, śakyasi tvaṃ taṃ bhagavantam asmākam upadarśayitum.
body.translated_text: Upon merely hearing this, her [the mother-in-law's] mind became filled with faith toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>. With a serene mind she said: 'Daughter, can you show that <s>Bhagavān</s> to us?'

body.text: sā kathayati: ārye, tena hi tvaṃ bhaktaṃ sajjīkuru, śvo 'haṃ bhagavantam ānayisyāmīti. mūṣilapatnī kathayati: sādhu, sarvaṃ sajjitam iti.
body.translated_text: She [<s>Sumāgadhā</s>] said: 'Venerable lady, then prepare a meal. Tomorrow I shall bring the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' <s>Mūṣila</s>'s wife said: 'Very well, everything is prepared.'

body.text: tataḥ sumāgadhā bhavanapṛṣṭham abhiruhya maṇḍalakam upalipya puṣpāṇy avakīrya bhagavantam abhinamasya yasyāṃ diśi prativasati tasyāṃ diśi puṣpāṇi kṣipati, dhūpaṃ ca dadāti, bhṛṅgārodakaṃ ca bhagavato nimantraṇakaṃ preṣayati. evam āha:
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sumāgadhā</s>, ascending to the rooftop of the house, plastered a circle, scattered flowers, bowed toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and toward the direction where he was dwelling she cast flowers and offered incense, and sent a water-pitcher as an invitation to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. She spoke thus:

body.text:
sarvajña kāruṇika bho khalu sāṃprataṃ me saṃdarśanaṃ svayam ihāgamanaṃ kurusva /
saṃghena sāgarasamena samaṃ jitāre āgāminīṃ prativasasva niśām atulyam //
anugrahārthaṃ bhagavan mamādya kartuṃ narāṇāṃ manasaḥ prasādaṃ /
rūpasya te darśanamātrakena lokaikanātha kriyatāṃ prasādaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'O Omniscient One, O Compassionate One, now grant me an audience by coming here yourself. Together with the <s>Saṅgha</s> vast as the ocean, O Conqueror, stay this coming night, O Incomparable One. For the sake of bestowing grace upon me today, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, to bring serenity to the minds of people, by the mere sight of your form, O sole lord of the world, bestow your grace.'

body.text: tatas tāni puṣpāṇi buddhānāṃ buddhānubhāvena devatānāṃ ca devatānubhāvena haṃsapaṅktir ivākāśe jetavanābhimukhāni saṃprasthitāni, dhūpo 'bhrakūṭavad vaiḍūryaśalākovedakaṃ bhagavato 'grataḥ sthitam.
body.translated_text: Then those flowers, by the power of the Buddhas and by the power of the deities, like a row of swans through the sky, set forth toward <s>Jetavana</s>.

body.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvāyuṣmān ānando bhagavantaṃ papracha: kuto bhagavann idaṃ nimantraṇakam āyātam.
body.translated_text: Seeing that, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'From where, <s>Bhagavān</s>, has this invitation come?'

body.text: puṇḍravardhanād, ānanda, ṣaṣṭyuttarād yojanaśatāt. gacchānanda, bhikṣūṇām ārocaya: śvo yuṣmābhiḥ puṇḍravardhanaṃ nagaraṃ gantavyaṃ, tirthyāvaṣṭabdhaṃ taṃ nagaram ṛddhivikurvaṇaṃ kartavyam, aprasannānāṃ prasādāya, prasannānāṃ bhūyobhāvāya, durmaṅkūnāṃ nirgrahāya, lajjināṃ sparśavihārāyeti.
body.translated_text: 'From <s>Puṇḍravardhana</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, a hundred and sixty <s>yojanas</s> away. Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, and announce to the monks: Tomorrow you must go to the city of <s>Puṇḍravardhana</s>.'

body.text: evaṃ bhadantety āyuṣmān ānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya gaṇḍīm ākoṭya bhikṣusaṃghaṃ saṃnipātya vṛddhānte sthitvā śalākāṃ cārayann evam āha: śṛṇvantu bhadantāh, saṃghaṃ bhagavān ājñāpayati.
body.translated_text: 'Very well, Venerable Sir,' said the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, and having assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, he struck the <s>gaṇḍī</s> (gong), assembled the community of monks, stood at the senior end, and distributed the voting sticks (<s>śalākā</s>).

body.text: śvo yuṣmābhiḥ puṇḍravardhanaṃ nagaraṃ gantavyaṃ, tīrthyāvaṣṭabdhaṃ taṃ nagaram, ṛddhivikurvaṇam kartavyam, aprasannānāṃ prasādāya, prasannānāṃ bhūyobhāvāya, durmaṅkūnāṃ nirgrahāya, lajjināṃ sparśavihārayeti.
body.translated_text: 'Tomorrow you must go to the city of <s>Puṇḍravardhana</s>. That city is occupied by <s>tīrthyas</s> (heretics). You must perform miraculous displays (<s>ṛddhivikurvaṇa</s>), to generate faith in those without faith.'

body.text: tataḥ sthavirasthavirāḥ śalākāṃ grahītum ārabdhāḥ. tatra pūrṇo nāma sukuṇḍopadhānīyaḥ sthaviraḥ, so 'pi śalākāṃ grahītum ārabdhaḥ. āyuṣmatānandenocyate: sthavira, nedam anāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhaṃ gantavyam, api tu puṇḍravardhanaṃ nagaraṃ gantavyaṃ ṣaṣṭyuttarayojanaśataṃ yāvad ṛddhivikurvaṇaṃ kartavyam.
body.translated_text: Then the senior elders began to take the voting sticks. Among them was an elder named <s>Pūrṇa Sukuṇḍopadhānīya</s>, and he too began to take a voting stick.

body.text:
tataḥ sasaṃbhramaṃ sthaviraḥ śalākāṃ chorayitvā, yāvad dvitīyasya bhikṣoḥ śalākā na dīyate, tāvat ṣaḍabhijñām utpādya gajabhujasadṛśaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ bāhum abhiprasārya śalākāṃ gṛhītvā kathayati:
na hi rūpaguṇair na hi sauṣṭhavair na balātkāraguṇair na gauravāt /
jarayā hi nipīḍitayauvanāḥ ṣaḍabhijñās tu bhavanti madvidhāḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the elder hastily cast aside his voting stick, and before the stick could be given to a second monk, he generated the six superknowledges (<s>ṣaḍabhijñā</s>) and departed.

body.text: tataḥ prabhatāyām rajanyāṃ sthavirasthavirāḥ svakasvakena ṛddhyanubhāvena saṃprasthitāḥ.
body.translated_text: Then, at dawn, the senior elders set forth, each by his own miraculous power.

body.text: atha mūṣilapatnī bhagavato 'rthe śuciṃ praṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ samudānīyāsanakāni prajñapya, udakamaṇiṃ pratiṣṭhāpya, bhavanapṛṣṭham abhiruhya, sumāgadhāpi svāminā sārdhaṃ śvaśureṇa bahiḥ sthitā cintayati.
body.translated_text: Now <s>Mūṣilapatnī</s> had prepared for the <s>Bhagavān</s> pure and excellent food, both hard and soft, arranged seats, and set out a water-purifying gem.

body.text: kiṃ bhagavān āgamiṣyati. atha nāgamisyatīti. athavānyatropanimantrito bhaviṣyati.
body.translated_text: 'Will the <s>Bhagavān</s> come? Or will he not come? Or perhaps he has been invited elsewhere.'

body.text: tato bhagavantaṃ namaskṛtya yasyāṃ diśi prativasati tām diśaṃ prekṣitum ārabdhā.
body.translated_text: Then, having paid homage to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, she began to look toward the direction in which he dwelt.

body.text: atrāntareṇāyuṣmān ājñātakauṇḍinya uragaratham abhinirmāya śanair mandaṃ mandaṃ deve vṛṣṭāyamāne vidyutsu niścarantīṣu meghadhvaninirnādena tatropaviṣṭa upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, the venerable <s>Ājñātakauṇḍinya</s>, having magically created a serpent-chariot, came slowly, gently, gently through the sky, as rain fell softly and lightning flashed among the clouds.

body.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sumāgadhāyāḥ svāmī sumāgadhāṃ papraccha: sumāgadhe, 'yaṃ te sa śāstā, yo 'yam uragarathopaviṣṭaḥ śanair mandaṃ mandaṃ deve vṛṣṭāyamāne vidyududdyotaṃ darśayamāno meghadhvaninirnādena ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Sumāgadhā's</s> husband asked <s>Sumāgadhā</s>: '<s>Sumāgadhā</s>, is this your teacher, the one seated on the serpent-chariot, coming slowly, gently?'

body.text: sā provāca: nāyam āryo 'jñātakauṇḍinyaḥ saṃghasthaviraḥ, anena bhagavatā bārāṇasyāṃ dharme deśyamāne tatprathamato vairāgyam adhigatam ayaṃ bhagavatā nirvāṇādhigamaprāptānām agro nirdiṣṭah, sa eṣāgacchati. (1)
body.translated_text: She replied: 'This is not he. This is the noble <s>Ājñātakauṇḍinya</s>, the elder of the <s>Saṃgha</s>. When the <s>Bhagavān</s> was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> at <s>Bārāṇasī</s> (Varanasi), he was the very first to attain detachment.'

body.text: atrāntareṇāyuṣmāñ chāriputraḥ siṃharatham abhinirmāya tatropaviṣṭa upari vihāyasā rddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, having magically created a lion-chariot and seated upon it, came through the sky by his miraculous power.

body.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sumāgadhāyāḥ svāmī sumāgadhāṃ papraccha: sumāgadhe, 'yaṃ te sa śāstā yo 'yaṃ siṃharathenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Sumāgadhā's</s> husband asked <s>Sumāgadhā</s>: '<s>Sumāgadhā</s>, is this your teacher, the one coming on the lion-chariot?'

body.text: sā kathayati: nāyam āryaḥ śāriputro, yo 'yaṃ bhagavatā prajñāvatām agro nirdiṣṭaḥ.
body.translated_text: She replied: 'This is not he. This is the noble <s>Śāriputra</s>, whom the <s>Bhagavān</s> has declared foremost among those endowed with wisdom.'

body.text: asya ca garbhasthasya mātrā jambūdvīpe sarvavādino nirgṛhītāḥ.
body.translated_text: 'While he was still in the womb, his mother defeated all debaters in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>.'

body.text: jananyāś cānena dauhadam utpāditam: apy evāhaṃ sumerumūrdhāruhya caturṇām api ratnākarāṇāṃ payaḥ pibeyam iti.
body.translated_text: 'And he caused his mother to have this pregnancy-craving: "Oh, that I might climb to the summit of <s>Sumeru</s> and drink the waters of all four oceans!"'

body.text: atha tiṣyena dvijapravareṇendrajālapāramiprāptaṃ harim indrajālācāryam āhūya narasurāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragagandharvayakṣasamavāye devyā dauhadaṃ vinītam.
body.translated_text: Then, <s>Tiṣya</s>, the foremost among Brahmins, summoned <s>Hari</s>, the master of illusion (<s>indrajāla</s>) who had attained the perfection of illusion, and brought together humans, gods, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s>.

body.text: asya ca mātuḥ kukṣiniṣkrāntasya pitrā sarvanaimittikāḥ samāhūyoktāḥ: paśyantu bhavantaḥ, kumārasya kiṃ prabhāvo bhaviṣyatīti.
body.translated_text: When he had emerged from his mother's womb, his father assembled all the astrologers and said: 'Behold, sirs! What will be the power of this boy?'

body.text: te cāvalokayitum ārabdhāḥ. kumārasya lakṣaṇodāratāṃ rūpodāratāṃ ca dṛṣṭvā paraṃ vismayam āpannā, na śaknuvanti vyākartuṃ kumārasyedaṃ prabhāvam iti.
body.translated_text: They began to examine him. Seeing the excellence of the boy's marks and the excellence of his beauty, they were filled with supreme wonder and were unable to pronounce a verdict.

body.text: athāmbaragatena mahābrāhmaṇā teṣām saṃśayam apanayanārthaṃ brāhmaṇasvareṇāvaghoṣitam.
body.translated_text: Then a great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> from the sky, in order to dispel their doubt, proclaimed in the voice of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>:

body.text: eṣa kumāraḥ śākyamuneḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhattvaṃ sākṣāt kariṣyati, sarvaśrāvakānāṃ cāgro bhaviṣyati, dharmacakrānuvartayitā.
body.translated_text: 'This boy, having gone forth in the teaching of <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, will realize <s>arhatship</s> through the abandonment of all defilements. He will be declared foremost among all <s>śrāvakas</s>.'

body.text: idānīṃ vādinaś cāsya mukhaṃ nirīkṣya cirakālābhilaṣitāṃ vācam api na niścārayanti, kaḥ punar vādo. vādakaraṇe ayaṃ bhagavatā evam uktaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Even now, debaters looking at his face cannot utter even a long-desired word, let alone engage in debate. He is the <s>Bhagavān</s> (the master) in the matter of debate.'

body.text: mahāsamudrapramāṇaṃ pūrṇamasibhājanasya, sumerupramāṇam bhūrjapatrabhārasya, caturdvīpeṣu sarvasattvadhātupramāṇaṃ lekhakānām, asyāḥ pṛthivyās tṛṇakāsṭhaśākhāparṇasadapramāṇaṃ kalamānāṃ parikṣayaṃ paryāyena gacchet, na tv evāsya śāriputrasya prajñāyāḥ kṣayaṃ vadāmi. ato mahāprajña ity ākhyātaḥ mahāsārthavāhavat.
body.translated_text: 'The measure of the great ocean is but a vessel of the full-moon, the measure of <s>Sumeru</s> is but a load of birch-bark leaves, the measure of all beings in the four continents is but the number of scribes —'

body.text:
yāvat sarvasattveṣu prajñā 'sya sarvotkṛṣṭā yāvat tribhuvavāsisakalanarāmarasurasya
sarvalokasya yā prajñā sthāpayitvā tathāgatam /
śāriputrasya prajñāyāḥ kalāṃ nārhati ṣoḍaśām //
body.translated_text: '— yet his wisdom is supreme among all beings. The wisdom of the entire world including all beings dwelling in the three realms, humans, gods, and demons, setting aside the <s>Tathāgata</s> —'

body.text: anyam apy uktam: caturāryasatyasaṃkṣepavistaravibhāgavidhikathāvasare nāsty utpattiṣv asya samo jagati pratyekabuddho 'pi, sa eṣāgacchati. (2)
body.translated_text: 'Moreover it is said: At the occasion of teaching the condensed, extended, and classified analysis of the Four Noble Truths, there is none equal to him in all existence, not even a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>.'

body.text: atrāntareṇāyuṣmān mahākāśyapaḥ sauvarṇaṃ parvatam abhinirmāya nānāmṛgagaṇopetaṃ nānāprasravākulaṃ nānāpakṣigaṇākīrṇaṃ nānāvṛkṣopaśobhitaṃ tatropaviṣṭaḥ sa upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, having magically created a golden mountain complete with various herds of animals, various streams, various flocks of birds, and various trees, came through the sky.

body.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sumāgadhāyāḥ svāmī sumāgadhāṃ papraccha: sumāgadhe, ayaṃ te sa śāstā yo 'yaṃ suvarṇam parvatam abhiruhyāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Sumāgadhā's</s> husband asked <s>Sumāgadhā</s>: '<s>Sumāgadhā</s>, is this your teacher, the one coming mounted on the golden mountain?'

body.text: sā kathayati: nāyam āryo mahākāśyapo, 'yaṃ bhagavatā alpecchānāṃ saṃtuṣṭānāṃ dhūtaguṇadharāṇām agro nirdiṣṭaḥ.
body.translated_text: She replied: 'This is not he. This is the noble <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, whom the <s>Bhagavān</s> has declared foremost among those of few desires, those who are content, and those who observe the ascetic practices (<s>dhūtaguṇa</s>).'

body.text: anenaikonaṃ lāṅgalasahasraṃ lakṣāhatānāṃ, ṣaṣṭihiraṇyakoṭyaḥ sauvarṇānāṃ, yavānām aśītibhiḥ khāryaṃ, ṣoḍaśa dāsagrāmam, aṣṭādaśa mahābhāktagrāmāḥ, anekaśatasahasrāṇi vastūny upakaraṇaṃ samutsṛjya pravrajitaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'He had nine hundred and ninety-nine ploughs that struck a hundred thousand (coins), sixty million gold coins, eighty measures of barley, sixteen slave-villages — (all of which he renounced).'

body.text:
punar aparaṃ: sarvaśrāvakānāṃ samakṣam ayaṃ bhagavatārdhāsanenopanimantritaḥ.
ekaprasthodanaṃ śreyaḥ, ekaśayyā sukhāvahā /
ekadūṣyayugaṃ vāryaṃ, geyo mohaparigrahaḥ //
iti kṛtvā, pratigṛhītāśeṣā yā aparigraha iti na gṛhītaḥ. yaś ca bhāgineyām abhirūpāṃ darśanīyāṃ janapadakalyāṇīsadṛśīṃ tām apahāya pravrajitaḥ, sa eṣāgacchati. (3)
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, he alone among all <s>śrāvakas</s> was invited by the <s>Bhagavān</s> with a half-seat: "One portion of food is better; one bed is happiness-bringing."'

body.text: atrāntareṇāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyana airāvaṇagajavaravilāsagāminaṃ paramasvabhāvalakṣaṇavyañjanopetapuṇyadarśanaṃ hastinam abhinirmāya tatropaviṣṭa upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, having magically created a great elephant with the graceful gait of <s>Airāvaṇa</s>, endowed with the supreme marks and signs of its true nature, beautiful with merit —

body.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sumāgadhāyāḥ svāmī papraccha: sumāgadhe, 'yaṃ te sa śāstā yo 'yaṃ nāgendrarathenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Sumāgadhā's</s> husband asked: '<s>Sumāgadhā</s>, is this your teacher, the one coming on the elephant-king chariot?'

body.text: sā kathayati: nāyam āryo mahāmaudgalyāyano, 'yaṃ bhagavatā ṛddhimatām agro nirdiṣṭaḥ.
body.translated_text: She replied: 'This is not he. This is the noble <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, whom the <s>Bhagavān</s> has declared foremost among those with miraculous powers (<s>ṛddhi</s>).'

body.text: anena śakrasya devānām indrasya vaijayantaḥ prāsādaḥ, yojanasahasraṃ samantāt, parikṣepeṇa caturaśītibhiḥ stambhasahasraiḥ supratiṣṭhitaḥ, ardhapañcemāni yojanāni devapurād atyudgataḥ pādāṅguṣthenābhikampitaḥ.
body.translated_text: By him, <s>Śakra's</s>, the lord of the <s>devas</s>', <s>Vaijayanta</s> palace — a thousand <s>yojanas</s> all around, well-established with eighty-four thousand pillars, rising four and a half <s>yojanas</s> above the city of the gods — was shaken with a mere toe.

body.text: nandopanandau nāma nāgarājānau sumerubhṛguṇapariveṣṭitaṃ kṛtvāvasthitau ca vinītau.
body.translated_text: The two <s>nāga</s> kings named <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s>, who had stationed themselves coiled around <s>Sumeru</s>, were subdued by him.

body.text: punar apy anena bhagavān evam uktaḥ: evaṃ hi bhadanta vaijayante durbhikṣaṃ kṛcchraṃ kāntāraṃ, durlabhaḥ piṇḍako yācanakena, bhikṣavo 'pi lūhabhojanena pariklāmyante.
body.translated_text: Furthermore, he addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: 'Indeed, venerable sir, in the <s>Vaijayanta</s> [palace] there is a famine, hardship, and a wilderness; alms are hard to obtain by begging, and the <s>bhikṣus</s> too are exhausted from meager food.'

body.text: saṃmukhaṃ me bhadanta bhagavato 'ntikāc chrutaṃ saṃmukham udgṛhītam: asyāṃ mahāpṛthivyāṃ pārthivaḥ praṇīto rasadhātuḥ: so 'dhastād avasthita iti.
body.translated_text: 'Face to face, venerable sir, I have heard from the <s>Bhagavān</s>, face to face I have received: in this great earth there is an excellent earth-essence (<s>rasadhātu</s>); it is situated below.'

body.text: tad icchāmy asyā mahāpṛthivyāḥ pārthivaḥ praṇīto rasadhātuḥ tam ūrdhvaṃ kartuṃ, yam ūrdhvaṃ tam adhaḥ kartum.
body.translated_text: 'I wish to raise upward the excellent earth-essence of this great earth that is below, and to bring down that which is above.'

body.text: bhagavān āha: kasmin sthāne sthitvā mahāpṛthivīṃ parivartayasīti.
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Standing in what place would you overturn the great earth?'

body.text: eṣa evam āha: cakravāḍamahācakravāḍābhyāṃ stāne mahāpṛthiviṃ parivartayiṣyāmi.
body.translated_text: He replied: 'Standing between <s>Cakravāḍa</s> and <s>Mahācakravāḍa</s>, I shall overturn the great earth.'

body.text: bhagavān āha: ye pṛthivīsaṃniśritāḥ prāṇinas tān kathaṃ kariṣyasīti. eṣa evam āha: ye pṛthivīsaṃniśritāḥ prāṇinas tān vāmena pāṇinoddhṛtya dhārayiṣyāmi, dakṣiṇena prāṇinā mahāpṛthivīṃ parivartayiṣyāmi. bhagavān āha: kā tava saṃjnā bhaviṣyati.
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What will you do with the living beings who depend on the earth?' He replied: 'I shall lift up with my left hand and hold the living beings who depend on the earth, and with my right hand I shall overturn the great earth.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What will be your perception?'

body.text: tadyathā, bhadanta, balavān puruṣaḥ kadalīpatraṃ parivartayan paramalaghusaṃjñī bhavati, evam evāhaṃ bhadanta, mahāpṛthivīṃ parivartayan paramalaghusaṃjñī bhaviṣyāmīti.
body.translated_text: 'Just as, venerable sir, a strong man turning a banana leaf has the perception of the utmost lightness — even so, venerable sir, I, turning the great earth, shall have the perception of the utmost lightness.'

body.text: sādhu sādhu, maudgalyāyana, śakyasi tvam anayā ṛddhyānenopāyena mahāpṛthivīṃ parivartayitum iti. sa eṣāgacchati. (4)
body.translated_text: 'Well done, well done, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>! You are indeed capable of turning the great earth with this supernatural power and this method.' He is approaching now. (4)

body.text: atrāntareṇāyuṣmān mahākātyāyanaḥ sphaṭikamayaṃ kūṭāgāram abhinirmāya marakatenācchāditaṃ nānāratnastambhopanibaddhaṃ pravālavedikopaśobhitaṃ, tatra paryaṇkaḥ prajñaptaḥ paṭikāstṛto goṇikāstṛtaś citrikāstṛtaś tūlikāstṛtaḥ, yāval lohitopadhānas, tatropaviṣṭa upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, having magically created a crystal mansion covered with emeralds, supported by pillars of various jewels, adorned with a coral balustrade — and within it a throne was prepared, spread with woolen cloth, spread with blankets, spread with quilted covers, spread with cushions, with a crimson pillow — sitting therein, he approaches through the sky above by supernatural power.

body.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sumāgadhāyāḥ svāmī sumāgadhāṃ papraccha: sumāgadhe, 'yaṃ te sa śāstā yo 'yaṃ sphaṭikamayaṃ kūṭāgāram abhinirmāya tatropaviṣṭa upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Sumāgadhā's</s> husband asked <s>Sumāgadhā</s>: '<s>Sumāgadhā</s>, is this your Teacher — he who, having magically created a crystal mansion, sits therein and approaches through the sky by supernatural power?'

body.text: sā kathayati: nāyam āryo mahākātyāyanaḥ, ayaṃ bhagavatā sūtrāntavaibhaṅgakānāṃ puṇyamaheśākhyānām agro nirdiṣṭaḥ, sa eṣāgacchati. (5)
body.translated_text: She replied: 'This is not he. This is the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>. He has been declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> as the foremost among those who expound the <s>sūtrānta</s> and <s>vaibhaṅga</s> teachings, the great lords of merit. He is approaching now.' (5)

body.text: atrāntareṇāyuṣmān mahākausṭhilo vrṣabharatham abhinirmāya tatropaviṣṭa upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, the venerable <s>Mahākauṣṭhila</s>, having magically created a bull-drawn chariot, sitting therein, approaches through the sky above by supernatural power.

body.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sumāgadhāyāḥ svāmī sumāgadhāṃ papraccha: sumāgadhe, 'yaṃ te sa śāstā yo 'yaṃ vṛsabharathenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Sumāgadhā's</s> husband asked <s>Sumāgadhā</s>: '<s>Sumāgadhā</s>, is this your Teacher — he who approaches on a bull chariot?'

body.text: sā kathayati: nāyam āryo mahākauṣṭhilo, 'yaṃ bhagavatālpecchānām agro nirdiṣṭaḥ.
body.translated_text: She replied: 'This is not he. This is the venerable <s>Mahākauṣṭhila</s>. He has been declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> as the foremost among those of few desires.

body.text: ayaṃ bhikṣūn evam āha: sātirekāṇi me, āyuṣmanto, 'śītivarṣāni pravrajitasya, nābhijānāmi sabrahmacāriṇām antikāt parikarma svīkartum antaśaḥ pṛṣṭhodgharṣaṇamātram api, sa eṣāgacchati. (6)
body.translated_text: He addresses the <s>bhikṣus</s> thus: "Venerable ones, I have been ordained for more than eighty years, and I do not recall ever having accepted a personal service from a fellow celibate, not even so much as a back-rub." He is approaching now.' (6)

body.text: atrāntareṇāyuṣmān upālī haimaṃ tālavanam abhinirmāya suvarṇapuṣpaphalopetaṃ vividhamanojñasvarasaṃyuktaṃ, tatrāsajjamānaśarīra ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, the venerable <s>Upāli</s>, having magically created a golden palm grove endowed with golden flowers and fruits, with various enchanting sounds — with his body unattached thereto, approaches through the sky by supernatural power.

body.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sumāgadhāyāḥ svāmī sumāgadhāṃ papraccha: sumāgadhe, 'yam te sa śāstā yo 'yaṃ haimaṃ tālavanam āśritya ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Sumāgadhā's</s> husband asked <s>Sumāgadhā</s>: '<s>Sumāgadhā</s>, is this your Teacher — he who, resting upon a golden palm grove, approaches through the sky by supernatural power?'

body.text: sā kathayati: nāyam ārya upālī, ayaṃ bhagavatā vinayadharāṇām agro nirdiṣṭaḥ.
body.translated_text: She replied: 'This is not he. This is the venerable <s>Upāli</s>. He has been declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> as the foremost among bearers of the <s>Vinaya</s>.

body.text: asya ca pañcamātrātraiḥ śākyakumāraśatair nānālaṃkāravibhūṣitaiḥ pravrajyamānaiḥ purastād vastrāṇām ābharaṇānāṃ ca mahān rāśiḥ kṛtaḥ.
body.translated_text: When five hundred <s>Śākya</s> princes, adorned with various ornaments, were going forth, a great heap of garments and ornaments was gathered before him.'

body.text: ayam āryaḥ saṃlakṣayati: ime tāvat kumārāḥ kulavibhavayauvanopetāḥ sphītāny antaḥpurāṇi sphītāṇi ca kośakoṣṭhāgārāṇy apāsya pravrajitum ārabdhāḥ, aham asmim alaṃkāramātreṇa sakto.
body.translated_text: 'This venerable one reflected: "These princes, endowed with family, wealth, and youth, having abandoned their flourishing inner chambers and flourishing treasuries and storehouses, have begun to go forth into homelessness — and I am attached to mere ornaments!"'

body.text: 'nena vyasanam āpatsyate iti tāṃ vibhūtiṃ kheṭapiṇḍam ivāpahāya pravrajya tatprathamataram arhattvam adhigataṃ, sa eṣāgacchati. (7)
body.translated_text: '"This will bring me calamity." Having cast off that wealth as if it were a ball of spittle, he went forth and was the very first among them to attain <s>Arhatship</s>. He is approaching now.' (7)

body.text: atrāntareṇāyuṣmān aśvajic chānteneryāpathena mattahastinaṃ damayati, pātrakaravyagrahasta upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, the venerable <s>Aśvajit</s>, with his calm deportment taming a maddened elephant, holding his bowl and staff in hand, approaches through the sky above by supernatural power.

body.text: taṃ dṛsṭvā sumāgadhāyāḥ svāmī sumāgadhāṃ papraccha: sumāgadhe, 'yaṃ te sa śāstā yo 'yaṃ śānteneryāpathena pātrakaravyagrahasta upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Sumāgadhā's</s> husband asked <s>Sumāgadhā</s>: '<s>Sumāgadhā</s>, is this your Teacher — he who, with calm deportment, holding his bowl and staff in hand, approaches through the sky by supernatural power?'

body.text:
sā prāha: nāyam āryo 'śvajic, chānteneryāpathena mattahastinaṃ damayati. asya sakāśād anayā gāthayā:
karmakleśahetukāraṇavatī lokasya nivṛttir yathā
karmakleśanivṛttikāraṇam api provāca tan nāyakaḥ /
yasmin janmajarāvipattiniyataṃ duḥkhaṃ na saṃtiṣṭhate
tat mokṣapravaraṃ sa cādivṛṣabho jñātvā svayaṃ bhāṣate //
śrutvā pūrvaṃ tīrthikasyāryeṇa śāriputreṇa śrotaāpattiphalam adhigatam ayaṃ bhagavatā smṛtimatām agro nirdiṣṭaḥ, sa esāgacchati. (8)
body.translated_text: She said: 'This is not he. This is the venerable <s>Aśvajit</s>, who tames maddened elephants with his calm deportment. It was from him, by means of this verse: "The <s>Nāyaka</s> (Leader) has proclaimed that just as the world's cessation has action and afflictions as its cause and condition, so too the cause of the cessation of action and afflictions; in whom the suffering bound by birth, old age, and calamity does not remain — that supreme liberation he, the foremost bull, having known, himself declares" — having heard this, the venerable <s>Ārya Śāriputra</s> first attained the fruit of stream-entry from a non-Buddhist ascetic. He has been declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> as the foremost among those possessed of mindfulness. He is approaching now.' (8)

body.text: atrāntareṇāyuṣmān pūrṇo maitrāyaṇīputraḥ sauvarṇaṃ padmam abhinirmāya sahasrapatraṃ śakaṭacakramātraṃ vaiḍūryadaṇḍaṃ vajrāṅkurakeśaraṃ tatropaviṣṭa upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, the venerable <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s>, having magically created a golden lotus with a thousand petals, as large as a cart-wheel, with a <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) stem and diamond sprouts and filaments — sitting therein, approaches through the sky above by supernatural power.

body.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sumāgadhāyāḥ svāmī sumāgadhāṃ papraccha: sumāgadhe, ayaṃ te sa śāstā yo 'yaṃ sauvarnaṃ padmam abhinirmāya sahasrapatraṃ śakaṭacakramātraṃ vaiḍūryadaṇḍaṃ vajrāṅkurakeśaraṃ tatropaviṣṭa upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Sumāgadhā's</s> husband asked <s>Sumāgadhā</s>: '<s>Sumāgadhā</s>, is this your Teacher — he who, having magically created a golden lotus with a thousand petals, as large as a cart-wheel, with a <s>vaiḍūrya</s> stem and diamond sprouts and filaments, sits therein and approaches through the sky by supernatural power?'

body.text: sā kathayati: nayām āryo pūrṇo maitrāyaṇīputraḥ, ayaṃ bhagavatā maitrāṇikānām agro nirdiṣṭaḥ, sa eṣāgacchati. (9)
body.translated_text: She replied: 'This is not he. This is the venerable <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s>. He has been declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> as the foremost among those who inspire loving-kindness. He is approaching now.' (9)

body.text: atrāntareṇāyuṣmān dravyo mallaputraś catūratnamayam parvataśikharam abhinirmāya nānāghaṇṭāravākīrṇaṃ nānādhvajapatākopaśohitaṃ tatropaviṣṭa upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, the venerable <s>Dravya Mallaputra</s>, having magically created a mountain peak made of four kinds of jewels, strewn with various bells, adorned with various banners and pennants — sitting therein, approaches through the sky above by supernatural power.

body.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sumāgadhāyāḥ svāmī sumāgadhāṃ: papraccha sumāgadhe, 'yaṃ te sa śāstā yo 'yaṃ catūratnamayaṃ parvataśikharam abhinirmāya nānāghaṇṭārāvakīrṇaṃ nānādhvajapatākopaśobhitaṃ tatropaviṣṭa upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Sumāgadhā's</s> husband asked <s>Sumāgadhā</s>: '<s>Sumāgadhā</s>, is this your Teacher — he who, having magically created a mountain peak made of four kinds of jewels, strewn with various bells, adorned with various banners and pennants, sits therein and approaches through the sky by supernatural power?'

body.text: sā kathayati: nāyam āryo dravyo mallaputro, 'yaṃ bhagavatā pratilayakānām agro nirdiṣṭaḥ, yo 'yaṃ saṃlayān bhikṣūn tathā pratisaṃlayaneṣu niyojayati, sa eṣāgacchati. (10)
body.translated_text: She replied: 'This is not he. This is the venerable <s>Dravya Mallaputra</s>. He has been declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> as the foremost among those who emerge from meditative attainment — he who assigns the <s>bhikṣus</s> to their respective meditative attainments after they have arisen. He is approaching now.' (10)

body.text: atrāntareṇāyuṣmān aniruddhaḥ sarvasauvarṇaṃ prāsādam abhinirmāya vaiḍūryapravālastambhopaśobhitaṃ nānāratnavicitraṃ vitānamālāviracitaṃ śatapatākopaśobhitaṃ tanmadhye, tatra cābhyantare niṣaṇṇa, upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, the venerable <s>Aniruddha</s>, having magically created an entirely golden palace, adorned with <s>vaiḍūrya</s> and coral pillars, variegated with various jewels, decorated with garland-canopies, graced with a hundred pennants — seated within its interior, approaches through the sky above by supernatural power.

body.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sumāgadhāyāḥ svāmī sumāgadhāṃ papraccha: sumāgadhe, 'yaṃ te sa śāstā yo 'yaṃ sauvarṇaṃ prāsādam abhinirmāya, tatra cābhyantare siṃhāsane niṣaṇṇa upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Sumāgadhā's</s> husband asked <s>Sumāgadhā</s>: '<s>Sumāgadhā</s>, is this your Teacher — he who, having magically created a golden palace, sits within on a lion-throne and approaches through the sky by supernatural power?'

body.text: sā kathayati: nāyam āryo 'niruddho, 'yaṃ bhagavatā divyacakṣuṣām agro nirdiṣṭaḥ.
body.translated_text: She replied: 'This is not he. This is the venerable <s>Aniruddha</s>. He has been declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> as the foremost among those with the divine eye.

body.text: anena bārāṇasyām upaviṣṭasya pratyekabuddhasyaikapiṇḍapratipādanena saptakṛtvaś cakravartirājyāni kāritāni, saptakṛtvo deveṣu trayastriṃśeṣu devānāṃ rājyaṃ kāritam.
body.translated_text: By his offering of a single alms-meal to a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> seated in <s>Bārāṇasī</s>, he obtained the sovereignty of a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) seven times, and seven times he obtained the lordship of the gods among the <s>Trayastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-Three) gods.

body.text: tenaiva karmāvaśeṣeṇāḍhye śākyakule jātaḥ, anekāni ca śatasahasrāni lakṣāhatasya hiraṇyasuvarṇasya rūpyasya cāpahāya pravrajitaḥ, pravrajito 'pi cāyaṃ lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātraśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇām.
body.translated_text: By the residue of that very <s>karma</s>, he was born into a wealthy <s>Śākya</s> family. Having renounced many hundreds of thousands [of coins], along with <s>lakṣas</s> (hundred thousands) of gold, silver, and coined gold, he went forth; and even after going forth, he is one who obtains robes, alms-food, bowls, bedding, seats, and medicines for the sick.'

body.text: punar asya māhātmyaṃ śṛṇu: māhānāma mātrābhihitaḥ. putra, rājñā ghaṇṭāvaghoṣanaṃ kāritaṃ, śākyaiḥ kulaikayā pravrajitavyam iti, sa tvaṃ pravraja.
body.translated_text: Furthermore, hear of his greatness: <s>Mahānāma</s> was addressed by his mother: 'Son, the king has caused the bell to be rung [proclaiming] that from each <s>Śākya</s> family one must go forth [as a monk]. You should go forth.'

body.text: sa kathayati: nāhaṃ pravrajāmi. yas te priyaḥ putraḥ sukhāsane upari prāsādatale tiṣṭhati, taṃ pravrājayasveti.
body.translated_text: He said: 'I will not go forth. Your dear son who sits above on the rooftop of the mansion in a comfortable seat — ordain him.'

body.text: mātā prāha: putra, puṇyamaheśākhyo 'sau, mā tena saha spardhāṃ kuru.
body.translated_text: The mother said: 'Son, that one is called <s>Puṇyamaheśa</s> (Lord of Great Merit) — do not compete with him.'

body.text: ambe, tvaṃ tasyābhiprasannā yenāsau puṇyamaheśākhyaḥ. adya tasya mā kiṃcit preṣayājñāsyāmi puṇyamaheśākhyo na veti.
body.translated_text: 'Mother, you are partial to him, which is why he is called <s>Puṇyamaheśa</s>. Today, do not send him anything — I will find out whether he is truly <s>Puṇyamaheśa</s> or not.'

body.text: putra, evaṃ pratyakṣīkuru.
body.translated_text: 'Son, prove it then.'

body.text: tayā riktapiṭharikābhiḥ piṭakaṃ pūrayitvā śuklena vastreṇācchādya mudrābhilakṣitaṃ kṛtvā preṣyadārikāhaste preṣitam, saṃdiṣṭaṃ ca: dārike, yadi tvāṃ pṛcchet kim atreti, vaktavyṃ na kiṃcid iti. sā tam ādāya saṃprasthitā.
body.translated_text: She filled a basket with empty containers, covered it with a white cloth, sealed it, and sent it by the hand of a servant girl, instructing her: 'Girl, if he asks you what is in it, say: nothing.' She set out carrying it.

body.text: śakrasya ca devānām indrasyādhastāt jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate. sa saṃlakṣayati: yena nāma upari pratyekabuddhaḥ piṇḍakena pratipāditaḥ, tasyādya kathaṃ bhojanena vighāto bhaviṣyati. bhojanopasaṃhāro 'sya kartavya iti. tenāsau piṭako nānāsūpikarabhojanopetasyāhārasya pūritaḥ.
body.translated_text: Now <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, whose <s>jñānadarśana</s> (knowledge-vision) operates below, observed: 'The very one who fed a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> above with alms-food — how could he today suffer a deprivation of food? His food must be provided.' And so he filled that basket with food accompanied by various prepared dishes.

body.text:
yāvad asau dārikā tam ādāyāniruddhasakāśaṃ gatā, tenoktā: dārike, kim atreti. sā kathayati: kumāra, na kiṃcid iti. aniruddhaḥ saṃlakṣayati: priyo 'haṃ mātuḥ, kim asau
riktaṃ preṣayiṣyati. nūnam atra kiṃ nāma bhojyabhojanaṃ prakṣiptam paśyāmas tāvad iti.
body.translated_text: When the servant girl brought it to <s>Aniruddha</s>, he asked her: 'Girl, what is in this?' She said: 'Young master, there is nothing.' <s>Aniruddha</s> thought: 'I am dear to my mother; would she send me something empty? Surely some kind of food has been placed in here — let me see.'

body.text: yāvad udghāṭitaṃ sarvaṃ tad udyānam anekopakaraṇasurabhigandhasaṃpūrṇaṃ vyavasthitam. yaṃ ghrātvāniruddhaḥ paraṃ vismayam upagataḥ: mātṛbhakto 'yam, anena mātur agrapiṇḍaḥ preṣitaḥ. saṃdiṣṭaṃ cāmba, pratidinam īdṛśaṃ bhojanaṃ preṣitum arhasīti.
body.translated_text: When it was opened, the entire garden-pavilion stood filled with the fragrance of manifold delicacies. Having smelled it, <s>Aniruddha</s> was overcome with the greatest wonder: 'He is devoted to his mother; he has sent her the first portion of food.' And he sent word: 'Mother, you should be so kind as to send such food every day.'

body.text: sā dṛṣṭvā paramavismayam upagatā. tayā mahānāmopadarśitaḥ: putra, dṛṣṭaṃ te. amba, dṛṣṭam. nanu tvaṃ mayā pūrvam evoktaḥ: punyamaheśākhyaḥ sattvo manuṣya subhago, mā tena saha spardhāṃ kurṣveti. sa eṣāgacchati.
body.translated_text: She, having seen [this], was overcome with the greatest wonder. <s>Mahānāma</s> was shown [the evidence]: 'Son, did you see?' 'Mother, I saw.' 'Did I not tell you before: the being named <s>Puṇyamaheśa</s> is a man of great fortune — do not compete with him? Here he comes now.'

body.text:
āha ca:
sauvarṇe suvimānamālaracite ratnaprabhālaṃkṛte
dhyāyī dhyānarato niṣadya virajobhadrāsane saṃyataḥ /
āyāty eṣa caladhvajoparacito āryāniruddho muniḥ
mukto mocayitā nimagnam avaśaṃ lokaṃ bhavāmbho nidhau // (11)
body.translated_text:
And it is said:
'Upon a golden, beautifully garlanded, jewel-adorned throne,
the meditator, delighting in <s>dhyāna</s>, seated on a dustless, auspicious seat, restrained —
here comes the noble <s>Aniruddha</s>, the sage, adorned with waving banners,
liberated, the liberator of the world sunk helplessly in the ocean of existence.' (11)

body.text: atrāntareṇāyuṣmān śroṇaḥ koṭīkarṇaḥ puṣpamaṇḍapam abhinirmāya tatropaviṣṭa upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, the venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭīkarṇa</s>, having created a flower-pavilion and seated therein, came through the sky above by means of supernatural power.

body.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sumāgadhāyāḥ svāmī sumāgadhāṃ papraccha: sumāgadhe, 'yaṃ te sa śāstā yo 'yaṃ puṣpamaṇḍapam abhinirmāya tatropaviṣṭa upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Sumāgadhā</s>'s husband asked <s>Sumāgadhā</s>: '<s>Sumāgadhā</s>, is this your teacher who, having created a flower-pavilion and seated therein, comes through the sky above by supernatural power?'

body.text: sā kathayati: nāyam āryaḥ śroṇaḥ koṭīkarṇo, 'yaṃ bhagavatā alparajaskajātīyānām agro nirdiṣṭaḥ.
body.translated_text: She said: 'This is not [the teacher]; this is the noble <s>Śroṇa Koṭīkarṇa</s>, who has been declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> as foremost among those belonging to the class of those with little dust [on their eyes].'

body.text: ayaṃ ratnaprayuktikayā karṇikayā karṇe āmuktikayā jātaḥ. mātāpitarau paraṃ vismayam āpannau.
body.translated_text: 'This one was born with earrings (<s>karṇikā</s>) of precious gems adorning his ears. His parents were overcome with the greatest wonder.'

body.text: asya pitrā balasenena sarvaratnaparikṣakān āhūyoktaḥ: ratnānāṃ mūlyam kuruta iti. te ratnānāṃ mūlyaṃ kartum ārabdhā, na śaknuvanti ratnānāṃ mūlyaṃ kartum.
body.translated_text: 'His father <s>Balasena</s> summoned all the gem-assessors and said: Determine the value of the gems. They began to determine the value of the gems but were unable to assess their worth.'

body.text: dharmatā khalu yasya ratnasya na śakyate mūlyaṃ kartuṃ, tasya koṭimūlyaṃ kriyate. te kathayati: gṛhapate, ekaikasya ratnasya koṭimūlyam iti.
body.translated_text: 'Indeed, it is the rule that a gem whose value cannot be determined is valued at one <s>koṭi</s> (ten million). They said: Householder, the value of each gem is one <s>koṭi</s>.'

body.text: jñātayaḥ kathayanti: kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti. ayam dārakaḥ koṭimūlyakaratnikayā karṇikayā karṇe āmuktikayā jātah, śravaṇe nakṣatre jātas, tasmād bhavatu dārakasya śroṇaḥ koṭīkarṇa iti nāma. sa eṣāgacchati. (12)
body.translated_text: 'The relatives said: What shall be the boy's name? This boy was born with earrings of gems worth a <s>koṭi</s> adorning his ears, and was born under the <s>Śravaṇa</s> constellation; therefore let the boy's name be <s>Śroṇa Koṭīkarṇa</s>.' Here he comes now. (12)

body.text: atrāntareṇāyuṣmān śronaḥ koṭiviṃśaḥ nānāpuṣpaphalasaṃpannavanagahanam abhinirmāya rajodhvastāyām pṛthivyām ākāśacaṅkrame caṅkramyamāna upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, the venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>, having created a grove endowed with various flowers and fruits, walking back and forth on a sky-promenade above the dust-covered earth, came through the sky above by means of supernatural power.

body.text: taṃ dṣṛṭvā sumāgadhāyāḥ svāmī sumāgadhāṃ papraccha: sumāgadhe, 'yam te sa śāstā yo 'yaṃ nānāpuṣpaphalopetam vanagahanam saṃśrityākāśacaṅkrame caṅkramyamāṇo 'bhyāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Sumāgadhā</s>'s husband asked <s>Sumāgadhā</s>: '<s>Sumāgadhā</s>, is this your teacher who, having created a grove endowed with various flowers and fruits, walks back and forth on a sky-promenade and comes [through the air]?'

body.text: sā kathayati: nāyaṃ śāstā, āryo 'yaṃ śroṇaḥ koṭīviṃśah. asya jātamātrasya pitrā viṃśatihiraṇyakoṭyaḥ avalehikāmūlye 'nupradattā, asya dine dine pañcakārṣāpaṇaśatāni sthālīpākārthe vyayam upagacchati.
body.translated_text: She said: 'This is not the teacher; this is the noble <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>. At his very birth, his father gave twenty <s>koṭis</s> of gold coins as the price of the birth-licking ceremony. Day by day, five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> are spent for the preparation of his meals.'

body.text: āyuṣmatā mahāmaudgalyāyanena cāsya sakāśāt piṇḍapātram ādāya bhagavate dattam. yasya gandhena sarvaṃ rājagṛhaṃ nagaram āpūritaṃ pātrāvaśeṣaṃ ca rājña bimbisāreṇāsvāditam, āsvādya ca paraṃ vismayam āpannaḥ kathayaty:
body.translated_text: 'And the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> took alms-food from his presence and gave it to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. By its fragrance the entire city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> was pervaded, and the remains of the bowl were tasted by King <s>Bimbisāra</s>. Having tasted it, he was overcome with the greatest wonder and said:'

body.text: ahaṃ bhadanta rājakule jātaḥ, rājā saṃvṛtto, nābhijānāmi kadācid evaṃvidham annam āsvāditaṃ pūrvam.
body.translated_text: 'Venerable sir, I was born in a royal family, I became a king, yet I do not recall ever having tasted such food before.'

body.text: asya pādatale caturaṅgulamātrāṇi suvarṇāni romāni jātāni.
body.translated_text: 'On the soles of his feet, golden hairs four finger-breadths [long] had grown.'

body.text: ayaṃ bhagavataḥ sakāśaṃ gantukāmaḥ pṛcchati: kiṃ bhagavān yānena gacchaty āhosvit padbhyām iti. apare kathayanti: padbhyām iti. sa eṣa kathayati: aham api padbhyāṃ gacchāmīti.
body.translated_text: 'This one, wishing to go to the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence, asked: Does the <s>Bhagavān</s> travel by vehicle or on foot? Others said: On foot. He then said: I too shall go on foot.'

body.text: tasya pauruṣeyair vastrāṇi pṛthivyām āstīrṇāni. eṣa pṛcchati: kiṃ bhagavān āstīrṇena gacchaty āhosvid anāstīrṇeneti. te kathayati: nāstīrṇeneti. eṣa kathayati: apanayata vastrāṇi, aham apy anāstīrṇena gacchāmīti. tair apanītāni.
body.translated_text: 'His servants spread cloths on the ground. He asked: Does the <s>Bhagavān</s> walk on spread [cloths] or without them? They said: Without them. He said: Remove the cloths; I too shall walk without them. They removed them.'

body.text: punar aparāṇi dūṣyavastrāṇi pṛthivyām āstīrṇāni. eṣa pṛcchati: kiṃ bhagavān dūṣyāstīrṇena gacchaty āhosvid anāstīrṇena. te prāhuḥ: nāstīrṇeneti. eṣa āha: apanayata dūṣyāṇi. tair apanītāni.
body.translated_text: 'Then other fine cloths were spread on the ground. He asked: Does the <s>Bhagavān</s> walk on fine cloth spread [on the ground] or without? They said: Without. He said: Remove the fine cloths. They removed them.'

body.text: kumāra, puṇyamaheśākhyaḥ. tato 'parāṇy amanuṣyāni divyavastrāṇi prādurbhūtāni. eṣa dṛṣṭvāha: apanayantu amanuṣyavastrāṇīti. tair apanītānī. anena pṛthivyāṃ pādo nyastaḥ. ṣaḍvikāraḥ pṛthivīkampo jātaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Young master, [he is called] <s>Puṇyamaheśa</s> (Lord of Great Merit). Then other divine, non-human cloths appeared. Seeing them, he said: Let the non-human cloths be removed. They were removed. He placed his foot on the earth. A great earthquake of six kinds occurred.'

body.text: bhagavān āha: ito, bhikṣava, ekanavatiṃ kalpam upādāya na kadācic chroṇeṇa koṭīviṃśenānastīrṇe pṛthivīpradeśe pādo nyastaḥ. etarhi nyasto dharmagauravāt, na tu puṇyakṣayāt.
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Monks, for ninety-one <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s> has never placed his foot on an uncovered part of the earth. Now he has done so out of reverence for the <s>Dharma</s>, not from exhaustion of merit.'

body.text: yenāyaṃ ṣaḍvikāraḥ pṛthivīkampo jātaḥ. ayaṃ bhagavatā ārabdhavīryāṇām agro nirdiṣṭaḥ. sa eṣāgacchati. (13)
body.translated_text: 'This is why the great earthquake of six kinds occurred. This one has been declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> as foremost among those who have exerted effort.' Here he comes now. (13)

body.text: atrāntareṇāyuṣmān pilindavatso haṃsaratham abhinirmāya tatropaviṣṭa upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, the venerable <s>Pilindavatsa</s>, having created a chariot drawn by swans and seated therein, came through the sky above by means of supernatural power.

body.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sumāgadhāyāḥ svāmī sumāgadhāṃ papraccha: sumāgadhe 'yaṃ te sa śāstā yo 'yaṃ haṃsarathenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Sumāgadhā</s>'s husband asked <s>Sumāgadhā</s>: '<s>Sumāgadhā</s>, is this your teacher who comes in a swan-chariot?'

body.text: sā kathayati: nāyam āryo pilindavatso, 'yaṃ bhagavatā karuṇāvihārāṇām agro nirdiṣṭaḥ.
body.translated_text: She said: 'This is not [the teacher]; this is the noble <s>Pilindavatsa</s>, who has been declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> as foremost among those who dwell in compassion (<s>karuṇāvihāra</s>).'

body.text: anena gaṅgābhihitā: kuśalītiṣṭhety. asya vacanasamanantaram eva gaṅgā sthitā, aṅkuśasaṃtāḍiteva dviradavadhūr na prahasati. so 'yam āgacchati. (14)
body.translated_text: 'He addressed the <s>Gaṅgā</s>: Stand still! And the very moment he spoke, the <s>Gaṅgā</s> stood still, like an elephant cow struck by a goad, not moving forward.' Here he comes now. (14)

body.text: atrāntareṇāyuṣmān udāyī aśvaratham abhinirmāya catūratnopaśobhitaṃ tatropaviṣṭa, upari vihayasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, the venerable <s>Udāyin</s>, having created a horse-chariot adorned with four kinds of jewels and seated therein, came through the sky above by means of supernatural power.

body.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sumāgadhāyāḥ svāmī sumāgadhāṃ papraccha: sumāgadhe, 'yaṃ te sa śāstā yo 'yam aśvaratham abhinirmāya catūratnopaśobhitaṃ tatropaviṣṭa upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Sumāgadhā</s>'s husband asked <s>Sumāgadhā</s>: '<s>Sumāgadhā</s>, is this your teacher who, having created a horse-chariot adorned with four kinds of jewels and seated therein, comes through the sky above by supernatural power?'

body.text: sā kathāyati: nāyam ārya udāyī ayaṃ bhagavatā kulaprasādakānām agro nirdiṣṭaḥ.
body.translated_text: She said: 'This is not [the teacher]; this is the noble <s>Udāyin</s>. He has been declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> as foremost among those who inspire faith in families.'

body.text: anena rājā śuddhodanaḥ śuklodano droṇodano 'mṛtodano dhautodanaś ca, gopikāmṛgajāyaśodharāpramukhāni ṣaṣṭistrīsahasrāṇi bodhisattvavirahāc chokasāgaranimagnās tābhis tābhiḥ śrutibhiś cittaprahlādanībhir vividhābhir vāgbhiḥ śokaṃ parityājitāni. so 'yam āgacchati. (15)
body.translated_text: 'He consoled King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, <s>Śuklodana</s>, <s>Droṇodana</s>, <s>Amṛtodana</s>, and <s>Dhautodana</s>, as well as the sixty thousand women headed by <s>Gopikā</s>, <s>Mṛgajā</s>, and <s>Yaśodharā</s>, who were sunk in an ocean of grief due to the separation from the <s>Bodhisattva</s> — with those and those heart-gladdening sayings and various words he caused them to abandon their grief.' Here he comes now. (15)

body.text: atrāntareṇāyuṣmān jyotiḥpālo mayūraratham abhinirmāya tatropaviṣṭa upari vihāyasā ṛddhykāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: In the meanwhile, the venerable <s>Jyotiḥpāla</s>, having magically created a peacock chariot and seated upon it, came through the sky by means of supernatural power.

body.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sumāgadhāyāḥ svāmī sumāgadhāṃ papraccha: sumāgadhe, 'yaṃ te sa śāstā yo 'yaṃ mayūraratham abhinirmāya tatropaviṣṭa upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Sumāgadhā</s>'s husband asked <s>Sumāgadhā</s>: '<s>Sumāgadhā</s>, is that your teacher—he who, having magically created a peacock chariot and seated upon it, comes through the sky by means of supernatural power?'

body.text: sā kathayati: nāyam āryo jyotiḥpālo, 'yaṃ bhagavatā divyamānuṣīśriyaṃ tyājayitvā pravrājitaḥ.
body.translated_text: She said: 'This is not [the <s>Buddha</s>]; this is the noble <s>Jyotiḥpāla</s>, whom the <s>Bhagavān</s> caused to renounce divine and human glory and go forth as a renunciant.'

body.text: asya snānaśāṭako 'bhyavakāśe śoṣito vāyunohyamāno rājño bimbisārasyopari patitaḥ. rājā kathayati: bhavanto, rājārham idaṃ vastraṃ, kutra etat. te kathayanti: deva, śrūyate rājño māndhātasya saptāhaṃ hiraṇyavarṣaḥ patita iti, devasyāpi vastravarṣaḥ patitum ārabdho, nacirād hiraṇyavarṣaḥ patiṣyatīti.
body.translated_text: 'His bathing cloth, dried in the open, was carried by the wind and fell upon King <s>Bimbisāra</s>. The king said: "Sirs, this garment is fit for a king—where is it from?" They said: "Your Majesty, it is heard that upon King <s>Māndhāta</s>, a rain of gold fell for seven days. Upon Your Majesty too, a rain of garments has begun to fall; before long, a rain of gold will fall."'

body.text: rājā kathayati: bhavanto jyotiṣko gṛhapatir bhagavatā vyākṛto divyamānuṣīśriyaṃ pratyanubhaviṣyatīti, idaṃ ca divyaṃ vastram ākāśāt patitam, sthāpayata, tasyaivāgatasya dāsyāma iti.
body.translated_text: 'The king said: "Sirs, the householder <s>Jyotiṣka</s> was prophesied by the <s>Bhagavān</s> to enjoy divine and human glory, and this divine garment has fallen from the sky. Keep it; we shall give it to him when he comes."'

body.text: te caivam ālāpaṃ kurvanti, ayaṃ ca rājñaḥ sakāśam āgatah.
body.translated_text: 'While they were thus conversing, he [<s>Jyotiṣka</s>] arrived in the king's presence.'

body.text: rājā kathayati: kumāra, tvaṃ bhagavatā vyākṛto divyamānuṣīśriyaṃ pratyanubhaviṣyasīti, idaṃ ca divyaṃ ākāśāt patitam, gṛhāṇeti.
body.translated_text: 'The king said: "Young man, you were prophesied by the <s>Bhagavān</s> to enjoy divine and human glory, and this divine [garment] has fallen from the sky—take it."'

body.text: tena hastaḥ prasāritaḥ. devānaya paśyāmīti. sa nirīkṣitum ārabdho yāvat paśyaty ātmīyaṃ snānaśāṭakam.
body.translated_text: 'He extended his hand. "Let the gods bring it; let me see." He began to examine it, and saw that it was his own bathing cloth.'

body.text: sa vipuṣpya kathayati: deva, madīyaḥ snānaśāṭako 'yaṃ vāyunopakṣipyehānīta iti.
body.translated_text: 'He laughed and said: "Your Majesty, this is my bathing cloth, carried here by the wind."'

body.text: rājā kathayati: kumāra, kiṃ tava divyamānuṣī śrīḥ prādurbhūtā. deva, prādurbhūtā. kumāra, yady evaṃ kimarthaṃ māṃ na nimantrayase. deva, nimantrito bhava. gaccha, bhaktaṃ sajjīkuru. deva, yasya divyamānuṣī śrīḥ prādurbhūtā, kiṃ tena sajjīkartavyam. nanu sajjīkṛtam evāgaccheti.
body.translated_text: 'The king said: "Young man, has your divine and human glory manifested?" "Your Majesty, it has manifested." "Young man, if so, why do you not invite me?" "Your Majesty, consider yourself invited." "Go, prepare a meal." "Your Majesty, for one whose divine and human glory has manifested, what need is there to prepare? It is already prepared—just come."'

body.text: sa jyotiṣkasya gṛhaṃ gatvā bāhyaṃ parijanaṃ dṛṣṭvā indriyāṇy utkṣipati. jyotiṣkaḥ kathayati: deva, kimartham indriyāṇy utkṣipasīti. sa kathayati: kumāra, vadhūjano 'yam iti kṛtvā. nāyaṃ vadhūjano, bāhyo 'yaṃ parijanaḥ. sa paraṃ vismayam āpannaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'He went to <s>Jyotiṣka</s>'s house, and seeing the outer retinue of women, he averted his eyes. <s>Jyotiṣka</s> said: "Your Majesty, why do you avert your eyes?" He said: "Young man, thinking these are the women of the household." "These are not the household women; this is the outer retinue." He was filled with great amazement.'

body.text: punar madhyamaṃ parijanaṃ dṛṣṭvā indriyāṇy utkṣeptum ārabdhaḥ. jyotiṣkaḥ kathayati: deva, kimartham indriyāṇy utkṣipasīti. rājā kathayati: kumāra, vadhūjano 'yam iti kṛtvā. deva, nāyam api vadhūjanaḥ, kiṃtu madhyamo 'yaṃ parijanah. sa bhūyasyā mātrayā paraṃ vismayam āpannah.
body.translated_text: 'Again, seeing the middle retinue, he began to avert his eyes. <s>Jyotiṣka</s> said: "Your Majesty, why do you avert your eyes?" The king said: "Young man, thinking these are the women of the household." "Your Majesty, these too are not the household women; rather, this is the middle retinue." He was filled with even greater amazement.'

body.text: tatra madhyamāyām dvāraśālāyāṃ maṇibhir upacitā bhūmiḥ. tasyāṃ matsyā udakapūrṇāyām iva yantraprayogenoparibhramanto dṛśyante. rājā praveṣṭukamo jalam iti kṛtvā upānahau moktum ārabdhaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'In the middle entrance hall, the floor was inlaid with gems. In it, fish appeared to be swimming about on the surface as if it were filled with water, through a mechanical contrivance. The king, wishing to enter and thinking it was water, began to remove his sandals.'

body.text: jyotiṣkaḥ kathayati: deva, kasyārthe upānahāv apanayasīti. kumāra, pānīyam uttaritavyam. deva, nedaṃ pānīyam, api tu maṇibhūmir eṣā. kumāra, ime matsyā uparibhramanto dṛśyante. deva, yantraprayogenaite paribhramanti. rājā na śraddadhāte tenāṅgulimudrā kṣiptā sā raṇaraṇāśabdena bhūmau patitā. tato rājā vismayam āpannaḥ.
body.translated_text: '<s>Jyotiṣka</s> said: "Your Majesty, why are you removing your sandals?" "Young man, [I must] cross the water." "Your Majesty, this is not water; it is a floor of gems." "Young man, these fish are seen swimming about on the surface." "Your Majesty, they move about by a mechanical contrivance." The king did not believe it, so he tossed his signet ring, which fell to the floor with a clinking sound. Then the king was amazed.'

body.text: praviśya siṃhāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ. tato vadhūjanaḥ pādābhivandaka upasaṃkrāntaḥ. tāsām aśrupāto jātaḥ. rājā kathayati: kumāra, kasmād ayaṃ vadhūjano roditi. deva, nāyaṃ roditi, kiṃtu devasya kāṣṭhadhūpena vastrāṇi dhūpitāni, tenāsām aśrupāto jāta iti.
body.translated_text: 'Having entered, he sat on a throne. Then the household women came forward to pay respect to his feet. Tears fell from their eyes. The king said: "Young man, why are these household women weeping?" "Your Majesty, they are not weeping; rather, Your Majesty's garments were perfumed with coarse incense, and from that their tears have arisen."'

body.text: rājā tatra tayā divyamānuṣikayā śriyā upacaryamāṇo na niṣkrāmati; rājakṛtyāni rājakaraṇīyāni parihātum ārabdhāni.
body.translated_text: 'The king, being served there by that divine and human glory, did not leave; royal duties and royal affairs began to be neglected.'

body.text: amātyair ajātaśatruḥ kumāro 'bhihitaḥ: kumāra, devo jyotiṣkasya gṛhaṃ praviśya pramattaḥ, gaccha, nivedayeti.
body.translated_text: 'The ministers told Prince <s>Ajātaśatru</s>: "Prince, the king has entered <s>Jyotiṣka</s>'s house and is engrossed. Go and inform him."'

body.text: tena gatvā ukto: deva, kiṃ tvam atra pariviśyāvasthito, rājakṛtyāni rājakaraṇīyāni parihīyanta iti.
body.translated_text: 'He went and said: "Your Majesty, why are you staying here absorbed? Royal duties and royal affairs are being neglected."'

body.text: rājā kathayati: kumāra, na śakto 'si tvam ekaṃ divasaṃ rājyaṃ kārayitum. devo jānīte, mamaiko divasaḥ praviṣṭasyati. adya devasya saptamo divaso vartate.
body.translated_text: 'The king said: "Young man, are you not able to conduct the kingdom for one day?" "The king would know—I have been here for one day." "Your Majesty, today is your seventh day."'

body.text: rājā jyotiṣkasya mukham nirīkṣya kathayati: kumāra, satyam. deva, satyam. saptamo divaso vartate.
body.translated_text: 'The king, looking at <s>Jyotiṣka</s>'s face, said: "Young man, is that true?" "Your Majesty, it is true. It is the seventh day."'

body.text: kumāra, kathaṃ rātriḥ prajñāyate divaso vā. deva, puṣpāṇāṃ saṃvikocavikāsān, maṇīnāṃ jvalanājvalanāt, śakunīnāṃ kūjanākūjanāt; santi tāni kusumāni yāni rātrau vikasanti na divā, santi yāni divā vikasanti na rātrau; santi te maṇayo ye rātrau jvalanti na divā, santi ye divā jvalanti na rātrau; santi te śakunayo ye rātrau kūjanti na divā, santi ye divā kūjanti na rātrau. rājā paraṃ vismayam āpannaḥ kathayati:
body.translated_text: '"Young man, how does one distinguish night from day?" "Your Majesty, by the closing and opening of flowers, by the blazing and non-blazing of gems, by the singing and non-singing of birds. There are flowers that bloom at night but not by day, and flowers that bloom by day but not at night. There are gems that blaze at night but not by day, and gems that blaze by day but not at night. There are birds that sing at night but not by day, and birds that sing by day but not at night." The king, greatly amazed, said:'

body.text: kumāra, avitathavādī bhagavān, yathā tvaṃ bhagavatā vyākṛtaḥ tathaiva nānyathety uktvā jyotiṣkasya gṛhān niṣkrāntaḥ.
body.translated_text: '"Young man, the <s>Bhagavān</s> is one who speaks truth. Just as you were prophesied by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, so it is and not otherwise." Having said this, he departed from <s>Jyotiṣka</s>'s house.'

body.text: ajātaśatrukumāreṇa jyotiṣkasantako maṇir apahṛtya dārakasya haste dattaḥ. tena yata eva gṛhītas tatraiva gatvāvasthitaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Prince <s>Ajātaśatru</s> stole a gem belonging to <s>Jyotiṣka</s> and placed it in a boy's hand. The gem left the hand and went back to the very place from which it had been taken.'

body.text: ajātaśatruḥ kathayati: dārakānaya taṃ maṇim, paśyāmīti. sa muṣṭiṃ vighāṭya kathayati: kumāra, kutra, na jāne kutra gata iti.
body.translated_text: '<s>Ajātaśatru</s> said: "Boy, bring me that gem; let me see it." He opened his fist and said: "Prince, where [is it]? I do not know where it has gone."'

body.text: sa tāḍayitum ārabdhaḥ. jyotiṣkaḥ kathayati: kumāra, kimartham enaṃ tāḍayasi. gṛhapate, 'haṃ caura, eṣa mahācauro, mayā tvadīyo maṇir apahṛtaḥ, so 'py anenāpahṛta iti.
body.translated_text: 'He began to beat [the boy]. <s>Jyotiṣka</s> said: "Prince, why are you beating him?" "Householder, I am the thief; this one is a great thief. I stole your gem, and he too has stolen it."'

body.text: sa āha: kumāra, na tvayāpahṛto, nāpy anenāpi tu yata eva tvayā gṛhītas tatraiva gatvāvasthito; 'pi tu, kumāra, svakaṃ te gṛhaṃ yāvadbhir maṇibhir anyena vā prayojanam tāvad gṛhāṇa yathāsukham iti.
body.translated_text: 'He [<s>Jyotiṣka</s>] said: "Prince, neither did you steal it, nor did he—rather, the gem went back to the very place from where you took it. But, prince, take as many gems as you need for your own house, or for any other purpose, at your pleasure."'

body.text: sa pratibhinnakaḥ saṃlakṣayate: yadā pitur atyayād rājā bhaviṣyāmi, tadā grahīṣyāmīti.
body.translated_text: 'He [<s>Ajātaśatru</s>], resentful, reflected: "When my father has passed away and I become king, then I shall take them."'

body.text: yadājātaśatruṇā devadattavigrāhitena pitā dhārmiko dharmarājo jīvitād vyaparopitaḥ, svayam eva ca paṭṭaṃ baddhvā rājye pratiṣṭhitaḥ, tadā tena jyotiṣko 'bhihito: gṛhapate, tvaṃ mama bhrātā bhavati, gṛhaṃ bhājayāma iti.
body.translated_text: 'When <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, instigated by <s>Devadatta</s>, had caused the death of his righteous father, the righteous king, and had himself tied on the royal fillet and established himself in the kingdom, then he said to <s>Jyotiṣka</s>: "Householder, you are my brother; let us divide the house."'

body.text: eṣa samlakṣayati: yena pitā dhārmiko dharmarājaḥ praghātitaḥ, sa mām marṣayatīti. kuta etan. nūnam ayaṃ madgṛham āgacchatu, kāmaṃ prayacchāmīti viditvā kathayati: deva, bibhaktam eva. kim atra vibhaktavyam. madīyaṃ gṛham āgaccha. ahaṃ tvadīyaṃ gṛham āgacchāmīti.
body.translated_text: 'He [<s>Jyotiṣka</s>] reflected: "He who caused the death of his righteous father, the righteous king—will he spare me?" How could that be? "Surely he should come to my house; I shall give him whatever he wishes." Having deliberated, he said: "Your Majesty, it is already divided. What is there to divide? Come to my house. I shall come to your house."'

body.text: ajātaśatruḥ kathayati: śobhanam, evam kuru. sa tasya gṛhaṃ gataḥ. eṣo 'pi ajātaśatror gṛhaṃ gatah. sā śrīs tasmād gṛhād antarhitā yatraiṣa jyotiṣkas tatraiva gatā. evaṃ yāvat sapta vārān antarhitā prādurbhūtā ca.
body.translated_text: '<s>Ajātaśatru</s> said: "Excellent, do so." He went to his [<s>Jyotiṣka</s>'s] house, and <s>Jyotiṣka</s> too went to <s>Ajātaśatru</s>'s house. But the glory vanished from that house and went to wherever <s>Jyotiṣka</s> was. Thus seven times it vanished and reappeared.'

body.text: ajātaśatruḥ saṃlakṣayate: evam api mayā na śakitaṃ jyotiṣkasya maṇīn apahartum, anyad upāyaṃ karomi.
body.translated_text: '<s>Ajātaśatru</s> reflected: "Even thus I have been unable to seize <s>Jyotiṣka</s>'s gems; I shall devise another stratagem."'

body.text: tena dhūrtapuruṣāḥ prayuktā: gacchata, jyotiṣkasya gṛhān maṇīn apaharateti.
body.translated_text: 'He dispatched rogue men: "Go, steal gems from <s>Jyotiṣka</s>'s house."'

body.text: te hi śiṭākarkaṭakaprayogenābhiroḍhum ārabdhāḥ. te 'ntaḥpurikayā upariprāsādatalagatayā dṛṣṭāḥ, tayā dhūrtadhūrtakā iti nādo muktaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'They began to climb up using a mechanism of stakes and hooks. They were seen by a woman of the inner quarters who was on the upper floor of the palace. She raised the cry: "Rogues! Rogues!"'

body.text: anena jyotiṣkena śrutam, anenāśayato vāg niścarita: tiṣṭhantu dhūrtakā iti. teṣāṃ yo yatrābhirūḍhaḥ, sa tatraivāsthitaḥ, yāvat prabhātā rajanī saṃvṛttā.
body.translated_text: '<s>Jyotiṣka</s> heard this, and from his sleep a voice issued forth: "Let the rogues stay [where they are]." Whoever had climbed up to wherever, he remained fixed right there, until the night passed and dawn broke.'

body.text: mahājanakāyena dṛṣṭās, te kathayanti: bhavanto 'nena kalirājena pitā dhārmiko dharmarājo jīvitād vyaparopita, idānīm gṛhāṇy api moṣayati, tat kiṃ na me muṣiṣyata iti. purakṣobho jātaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'The great crowd of people saw them. They [the rogues] said: "Sirs, this wicked king has caused the death of his righteous father, the righteous king, and now he is robbing [people's] houses too. Will he not rob us as well?" A public uproar arose.'

body.text: ajātaśatruṇāsya jyotiṣkasya dūto 'nupreṣito: muñcata, mamāyaṃ khalīkāra iti.
body.translated_text: '<s>Ajātaśatru</s> sent a messenger to <s>Jyotiṣka</s>: "Release them; this was my mischief."'

body.text: anena jyotiṣkenāśayato vāg niścāritā: gacchantu dhūrtakā iti. te gatāḥ.
body.translated_text: Then this <s>Jyotiṣka</s>, with intentional speech, uttered: 'Let the scoundrels go!' And they departed.

body.text: athaiṣa jyotiskaḥ saṃlakṣayate: yena nāma pitā jīvitād vyaparopitaḥ, sa māṃ na praghātayisyatīti. kuta etat. sarvathāhaṃ bhagavatā vyākṛto: mama śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhattvaṃ sākṣāt kariṣyatīti. gacchāmi, pravrajāmīti.
body.translated_text: Then this <s>Jyotiṣka</s> reflected: 'He who killed my father from his life — he will not have me killed. Why is this? In any case, I have been prophesied by the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "Having gone forth in my teaching, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), he will directly realize <s>arhatship</s>." I shall go and take ordination.'

body.text: anena sarvaṃ dhanajātaṃ dīnānathakṛpaṇebhyo dattam, adhanāḥ sadhanā vyavasthāpitāḥ. sa eṣāgacchati. (16)
body.translated_text: He gave all his wealth to the poor, destitute, and wretched, establishing those without wealth as those with wealth. And so he comes. (16)

body.text: atrāntareṇāyuṣmān kapphiṇo vicitraratnācalam abhinirmāya tatropaviṣṭa upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, the venerable <s>Kapphiṇa</s>, having magically created a mountain of various jewels, seated upon it, came through the sky by means of supernatural power.

body.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sumāgadhāyāḥ svāmī sumāgadhāṃ papraccha: sumāgadhe, 'yaṃ te sa śāstā yo 'yaṃ vicitraratnācalam abhinirmāya tatropaviṣṭa upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Sumāgadhā's</s> husband asked <s>Sumāgadhā</s>: '<s>Sumāgadhā</s>, is this your Teacher — he who, having magically created a mountain of various jewels, seated upon it, comes through the sky by means of supernatural power?'

body.text: sā kathayati: nāyam āryaḥ kapphiṇo, yo 'yaṃ bhagavatā vigatamadadarpāṇām agro nirdiṣṭaḥ.
body.translated_text: She replied: 'This is not [the Teacher]. This is the noble <s>Kapphiṇa</s>, whom the <s>Bhagavān</s> has declared foremost among those free from intoxication and pride.'

body.text: yo 'yaṃ rājā mahākapphiṇa ekasmin samaye aṣṭādaśāmātyasahasraparivṛto mṛgavadhāya nirgataḥ.
body.translated_text: 'He who was the great king <s>Kapphiṇa</s>, who once went out hunting, accompanied by eighteen thousand ministers.'

body.text: purastāt pṛṣṭhataś ca sarvabalaugham avalokyāmātyān āmantrayate: asti, bhavantaḥ, kasyacid evaṃrūpo balaughas tadyathā mamaitarhīti. te kathayanti: deva, nānyasya kasyacit.
body.translated_text: 'Looking at all his army-force in front and behind, he addressed the ministers: "Sirs, does anyone else have such an army-force as mine at this time?" They replied: "Your Majesty, no one else does."'

body.text: yāvad anena mahākapphiṇena rājñā śrāvastyādiṣu ṣaṭsu mahānagareṣu dūtaṃ preṣitam: yad vyutthitā bhavatha nopaveṣṭavyaṃ, śīghram āgantavyam; anyathā ced uttamena daṇḍena samanuśāsiṣyāmīti.
body.translated_text: 'Thereupon the great king <s>Kapphiṇa</s> sent a messenger to the six great cities beginning with <s>Śrāvastī</s>: "Once you have risen, you shall not sit down again; you must come quickly. Otherwise, I shall discipline you with the supreme punishment."'

body.text: etad vacanam upaśrutya ṣaṇmahānagaravāsino rājāno bhītās trastāḥ saṃvignāḥ samāgamya śrāvastīṃ gatvā bhagavate etad vṛttāntaṃ nivedayanti.
body.translated_text: 'Upon hearing this message, the kings dwelling in the six great cities, frightened, terrified, and alarmed, gathered together, went to <s>Śrāvastī</s>, and reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.'

body.text: bhagavatā te samāśvāsitā, uktāś ca: sa dūto matsakāśam ānetavya iti. tair dūtasya niveditam: asty asmākam rājādhirājas, taṃ tāvat paśyeti.
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> reassured them and said: "That messenger should be brought to me." They informed the messenger: "There is our supreme king — go see him first."'
