body.text: bhagavatā jetavanam catūratnamayaṃ nirmitaṃ devānām iva sudarśanaṃ nagaraṃ catvāro mahārājā dauvārikāḥ sthāpitāḥ, airāvatasadṛśā hastino, bālāhakasadṛśā, nandīghoṣasadṛśā rathā, vyāḍayakṣasadṛśā manuṣyāḥ, svayaṃ ca bhagavāṃś cakravartiveśam ātmānam abhinirmāya saptatālodgate mahāratnasiṃhāsane niṣaṇnāḥ.
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> magically created <s>Jetavana</s> made of four kinds of jewels, like the divine city <s>Sudarśana</s>; the Four Great Kings were stationed as doorkeepers; elephants like <s>Airāvata</s>, horses like <s>Bālāhaka</s>, chariots like <s>Nandīghoṣa</s>, men like <s>Vyāḍayakṣa</s> [were created]; and the <s>Bhagavān</s> himself, having magically created for himself the appearance of a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), sat upon a great jeweled lion-throne seven palm-trees high.'

body.text: dūtas tathāvidhāṃ śobhāṃ dṛṣṭvā paraṃ vismayam āpannaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'The messenger, seeing such splendor, was filled with supreme wonder.'

body.text: bhagavatā lekhaṃ likhayitvābhihitaḥ: kapphiṇo madvacanād vaktavyo lekhavācasamakalam eva: yat vyutthito bhavasi nopaveṣṭavyaṃ, śīghram āgantavyam, atha nāgacchasi, aham eva mahatā balaughena sārdham āgamiṣyamīti.
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> had a letter written and said: "Tell <s>Kapphiṇa</s> in my words, at the very moment of reading the letter: 'Once you have risen, you shall not sit down again; you must come quickly. If you do not come, I myself shall come with a great army-force.'"'

body.text: dūtena mahākapphiṇasya tat sarvaṃ saṃdiṣṭaṃ niveditam.
body.translated_text: 'The messenger conveyed and reported all this to <s>Mahākapphiṇa</s>.'

body.text: ayaṃ kapphiṇo rājāṣṭādaśāmātyasahasraparivṛtaḥ śrāvastīm anupraveśya jetavanaṃ praviṣṭaḥ, sahadarśanād asya yo rūpe rūpamada aiśvarye aiśvaryamadaḥ sa prativigataḥ, baladarpo 'dyāpi vadhyata eva.
body.translated_text: 'This King <s>Kapphiṇa</s>, accompanied by eighteen thousand ministers, entered <s>Śrāvastī</s> and went to <s>Jetavana</s>. At the very moment of seeing [the Bhagavān], whatever pride he had in his own beauty, whatever pride in his sovereignty — that vanished; but his pride in military strength was not yet destroyed.'

body.text: tato bhagavatā laukikaṃ cittam utpāditam: aho bata, śakro devānām indra aindraṃ dhanur ādāyāgacched iti.
body.translated_text: 'Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> produced a worldly thought: "Ah, would that <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, would come bearing <s>Indra's</s> bow!"'

body.text: sahacittotpādād bhagavataḥ śakro devānām indraḥ sārathiveśenaindraṃ dhanur upanāmitavān. tato bhagavatā tad dhanur upanāmitam. tad utkṣeptum api na śaknoti, kutaḥ punar āropayitum.
body.translated_text: 'At the very moment of the <s>Bhagavān's</s> thought, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, in the guise of a charioteer, offered <s>Indra's</s> bow. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> took up that bow. [<s>Kapphiṇa</s>] could not even lift it, let alone string it.'

body.text: tato bhagavatā saptāyomayyo bheryo nirmitāḥ, svayam eva tad dhanur ardhacandrākāreṇāropya śaraḥ kṣipto yena saptāyomayyo bheryaś chidrīkṛtās, tataḥ śabdo nirgataḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> created seven iron drums, and himself, having strung that bow in the shape of a half-moon, shot an arrow that pierced all seven iron drums; then a sound issued forth:'

body.text:
ārabhadhvam, niṣkrāmata, yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane /
dhūnīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāraṃ iva kuñjaraḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Strive, go forth, engage yourselves in the <s>Buddha's</s> teaching! / Scatter the army of <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death) as an elephant scatters a reed hut!'

body.text:
yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati /
prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyatīti //
body.translated_text: 'For whoever shall practice diligently in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, / having abandoned the cycle of birth, shall make an end of suffering.'

body.text: sa ca śabdo yāvad akaniṣṭhān devān gataḥ, tato 'sya yo 'bhūd baladarpaḥ sa prativigataḥ.
body.translated_text: 'That sound reached as far as the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods; thereupon his pride in military strength vanished.'

body.text: tato bhagavatāsya cittam ājñāya rājaveśam antardhāpya dharmo deśitah. yenāṣṭādaśāmātyasahasraparivāreṇa yāvac chrotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣāt kṛtavān, tato dṛṣṭasatyaś ca bhagavataḥ śāsane pravrajitaḥ. so 'yam āgaccati. (17)
body.translated_text: 'Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having discerned his mind, caused the royal attire to vanish and taught the <s>Dharma</s>. Together with his retinue of eighteen thousand ministers, he directly attained the fruit of stream-entry (<s>śrotaāpattiphala</s>). Then, having seen the truth, he went forth in the <s>Bhagavān's</s> teaching. He is the one who now comes.' (17)

body.text: atrāntareṇāyuṣmān ānandaḥ haṃsakrauñcamayūraśukasārikākokilajīvaṃjīvakanādopakūjitam ārāmam abhinirmāya tatropaviṣṭa upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having magically created a garden resounding with the calls of swans, herons, peacocks, parrots, <s>sārikā</s> birds, cuckoos, and <s>jīvaṃjīvaka</s> birds, seated upon it, came through the sky by means of supernatural power.

body.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sumāgadhāyāḥ svāmī sumāgadhāṃ papraccha: sumāgadhe, 'yaṃ te sa śāstā yo 'yaṃ haṃsakrauñcamayūraśukasārikākokilajīvaṃjīvakanādopakūjitam ārāmam abhinirmāya tatropaviṣṭa upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Sumāgadhā's</s> husband asked <s>Sumāgadhā</s>: '<s>Sumāgadhā</s>, is this your Teacher — he who, having magically created a garden resounding with the calls of swans, herons, peacocks, parrots, <s>sārikā</s> birds, cuckoos, and <s>jīvaṃjīvaka</s> birds, seated upon it, comes through the sky by means of supernatural power?'

body.text: sā kathayati: nāyam ārya ānandaḥ, ayaṃ ca bhagavatā indriyaguptadvārāṇām agro nirdiṣṭaḥ.
body.translated_text: She replied: 'This is not [the Teacher]. This is the noble <s>Ānanda</s>, and he has been declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> foremost among those whose sense-doors are guarded.'

body.text: ayaṃ ca bhagavataś caturbhir aṅgulair ūnaḥ suvarṇavarṇo dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'He is shorter than the <s>Bhagavān</s> by four finger-breadths, is golden-hued, and adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>).'

body.text: anena kāśyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya stūpe madhyamaṃ chattram āropitam. tasya karmaṇo vipākenārdhatṛtīyāni cakravartirājyasahasrāṇi; yady etarhi na pravrajito 'bhaviṣyad etarhi apy anena balacakravartirājyam akariṣyat.
body.translated_text: 'He placed the middle parasol upon the <s>stūpa</s> of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One. As the fruit of that deed, [he obtained] two and a half thousand <s>cakravartin</s> sovereignties. Had he not gone forth at this time, even now he would have exercised sovereignty as a powerful <s>cakravartin</s>.'

body.text: ayaṃ ca bhagavatā balāt pravrajitaḥ. ayaṃ ca bhagavato mātṛsvasāputro bhrātā bhavati. sa eṣāgacchati. (18)
body.translated_text: 'He was ordained by the <s>Bhagavān</s> forcibly. He is the <s>Bhagavān's</s> maternal aunt's son and his brother. He is the one who now comes.' (18)

body.text: atrāntarenāyuṣmān rāhulaś cakravartiveśam abhinirmāya saptaratnasamanvāgataś caturaśītyā bhaṭabalāgrakoṭibhiḥ samanugamyamānaś caturaśītyā nāgasahasrair upoṣadhanāgarājapramukhaiś caturaśītyāśvasahasrair bālāhakāśvarājapramukhair caturaśītyā rathasahasrair nandīghoṣarathapramukhair anekaiś ca paurajānapadasahasrair nānāpaṭahaśaṅkhabherīninādair ucchritadhvajapatākopaśobhitam abhinirmāya tatropaviṣṭa upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, the venerable <s>Rāhula</s>, having magically created the appearance of a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), endowed with the seven treasures, accompanied by eighty-four <s>koṭis</s> of elite soldiers, eighty-four thousand <s>nāgas</s> led by <s>Upoṣadha</s> the <s>nāga</s>-king, eighty-four thousand horses led by <s>Bālāhaka</s> the horse-king, eighty-four thousand chariots led by the <s>Nandīghoṣa</s> chariot, and many thousands of townspeople and countryfolk, with the sounds of various drums, conches, and kettle-drums, adorned and beautified with raised banners and flags, seated upon [this display], came through the sky by means of supernatural power.

body.text: taṃ dṛsṭvā sumāgadhāyāḥ svāmī sumāgadhāṃ papraccha: sumāgadhe, 'yaṃ te sa śāstā, yo 'yaṃ cakravartiveśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Sumāgadhā's</s> husband asked <s>Sumāgadhā</s>: '<s>Sumāgadhā</s>, is this your Teacher — he who comes in the guise of a <s>cakravartin</s>?'

body.text: sā kathayati: nāyam āryo rāhulo, 'yaṃ bhagavatā śikṣakāmānām agro nirdiṣṭaḥ.
body.translated_text: She replied: 'This is not [the Teacher]. This is the noble <s>Rāhula</s>, whom the <s>Bhagavān</s> has declared foremost among those eager for training.'

body.text: bhagavataḥ putro 'yaṃ pitur ujjhitāṃ śriyam uddyotamānaḥ, sarvacakravartiprativiśiṣṭatarām ṛddhim upadarśayann upari vihāyasā ṛddhyākāśenāgacchati.
body.translated_text: 'He is the son of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, illuminating the glory abandoned by his father, displaying supernatural power surpassing even that of all <s>cakravartins</s>, flying through the sky by means of supernatural power.'

body.text:
āha ca:
lakṣmīṃ lakṣaṇamālinīṃ surucirāṃ śakrarddhivispardhanīṃ
nāgānīkabalānvitāṃ sumahatīṃ ratnair vṛtāṃ saptabhiḥ /
kṛtvā buddhasuto 'bhyupaiti nabhasā veśaṃ ca rājñām ayaṃ
nāmnā rāhula ity aveti sumahate sampūjyamānaḥ suraiḥ //
body.translated_text:
And she said:
'Having assumed the royal appearance, endowed with the beauty of marks, supremely lovely, rivaling <s>Śakra's</s> splendor, / accompanied by <s>nāga</s>-army forces, supremely great, adorned with the seven treasures — / the <s>Buddha's</s> son approaches through the sky; this one bears the royal guise, / known by name as <s>Rāhula</s> — greatly honored by the gods.'

body.text:
bhittvorvīṃ jalavat prayānti munayaḥ kecit sṛjanto 'nalaṃ
ramyatoyadharā ivāśu jagati spaṣṭaṃ kṣaranto jalam /
śakrabrahmakuberavigrahadharāś candrārkadaityatviṣo
lokasyodayakāṅkṣiṇo hi nabhasā saṃprasthitāḥ sūratāḥ //
sa eṣāgacchati. (19)
body.translated_text: 'Some sages penetrate the earth like water, others emit fire; / like beautiful rain-clouds they swiftly shower water clearly upon the world. / Bearing the forms of <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Kubera</s>, with the radiance of moon, sun, and <s>daityas</s>, / desiring the welfare of the world, they have set forth through the sky — the heroes.' He is the one who now comes. (19)

body.text: saṃprasthitesu bhikṣusaṃghesu atrāntareṇa tathāgatapraveśaḥ. bhagavāṃs tathārūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpanno, yathāsamāhite citte bhagavataḥ kāyād raśmayo niścaranti, tadyathā nīlapītalohitāvadātamañjiṣṭhasphaṭikavarṇaḥ, yair ayaṃ loke udāreṇāvabhāsenāvabhāsito yāvac ca śrāvastīṃ yāvac ca puṇḍravardhanaṃ nagaram.
body.translated_text: After the communities of monks had set forth, meanwhile the <s>Tathāgata</s> made his entrance. The <s>Bhagavān</s> entered such a <s>samādhi</s> that, while his mind was concentrated, rays issued from the <s>Bhagavān's</s> body — blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, and crystal-colored — by which this world was illuminated with a magnificent radiance, extending as far as <s>Śrāvastī</s> and the city of <s>Puṇḍravardhana</s>.

body.text: atrāntareṇa sarve lokā bhagavantam abhiniṣkramantaṃ paśyanti, mahāṃś ca pṛthivīcālo babhūva.
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, all the worlds beheld the <s>Bhagavān</s> coming forth, and a great earthquake occurred.

body.text: atha brahmā sahāṃpatir bhagavataś cetasā cittam ājñāya sārdhaṃ rūpāvacarair devair āgatya bhagavato dakṣiṇe pārśve vyavasthitaḥ.
body.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, having discerned the <s>Bhagavān's</s> mind with his own mind, together with the gods of the <s>Rūpāvacara</s> (form realm), came and stood at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> right side.

body.text: śakro 'pi devānām indraḥ sārdhaṃ kāmāvacarair devair āgatya vāme pārśve vyavasthitaḥ.
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> too, the lord of the gods, having come together with the gods of the <s>Kāmāvacara</s> (desire realm), stood at the left side.

body.text: tumburusupriyapramukhāni pañcamātrāṇi gandharvaśatāny āgatya bhagavato 'grato vividhair vādyagītanṛttaviśeṣair upasthānaṃ kurvanto gacchanti.
body.translated_text: Five hundred <s>gandharvas</s> headed by <s>Tumburu</s> and <s>Supriya</s>, having come before the <s>Bhagavān</s>, proceed performing attendance with various special instrumental music, songs, and dances.

body.text: anekāni ca devatāśatasahasrāṇi pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti.
body.translated_text: And many hundreds of thousands of deities follow along close behind.

body.text: upariṣṭāc ca bhagavato 'psaraso divyāny utpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkamāndāravāṇi puṣpāṇi, divyāny agarucūrṇāni tagaracūrṇāni candanacūrṇāni tamālapattracūrṇani, divyāni ca vādyāni saṃpravādayanti, cailavikṣepāṃś cākārṣuh.
body.translated_text: And above the <s>Bhagavān</s> the <s>apsarases</s> [scatter] divine <s>utpala</s>, <s>padma</s>, <s>kumuda</s>, <s>puṇḍarīka</s>, and <s>māndārava</s> flowers, divine powders of <s>agaru</s> (aloe-wood), <s>tagara</s>, <s>candana</s> (sandalwood), and <s>tamāla</s>-leaf, and they sound divine instruments together, and they waved their garments.

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayenānyatarasmin araṇyāyatane sapta ṛṣisahasrāṇi prativasanti.
body.translated_text: Now at that time, in a certain forest tract, seven thousand <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers) were dwelling.

body.text: adrākṣus te ṛṣayo buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātrimśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam, aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ, sūryaprabhātirekaprabhaṃ, jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvatam, samantato bhadrakaṃ, havyāvasiktam iva hutavaham, kāñcanabhājanastham iva pradīpaṃ, suvarṇayūpam iva śriyā jvalantam.
body.translated_text: Those <s>ṛṣis</s> beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>), his body resplendent with the eighty secondary marks (<s>anuvyañjana</s>), adorned with a fathom-wide aura, his radiance surpassing the splendor of the sun, like a moving mountain of jewels, beautiful on every side, like a sacrificial fire sprinkled with oblations, like a lamp set in a golden vessel, blazing with splendor like a golden sacrificial post.

body.text: na tathā dvādaśavarṣābhyastaḥ śamathacittasya kalyatāṃ janayati, rājyābhinandino vā tatprathamato rājyābhiṣekaḥ, aputrasya vā putrapratilambhaḥ, daridrasya vā nidhidarśanaṃ, yathāvāropitaṃ kuśalamūlānāṃ tatprathamato buddhadarśanam.
body.translated_text: Not even twelve years' practice produces such fitness of a mind of <s>śamatha</s> (calm), nor [does] the first royal consecration of one longing for kingship, nor the obtaining of a son for the sonless, nor the sight of a treasure for the poor, as does — for those who have planted wholesome roots accordingly — the very first sight of the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: atha te ṛṣayo yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntā, upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte tasthuḥ.
body.translated_text: Then those <s>ṛṣis</s> approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and having approached and venerated the <s>Bhagavān's</s> feet with their heads, they stood to one side.

body.text: tato bhagavatā teṣām ṛṣīṇām āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikā dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā tair ṛṣibhir viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhittvā śrotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣāt kṛtam.
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having known the disposition and underlying tendency, the [mental] element and the nature of those <s>ṛṣis</s>, gave such a <s>Dharma</s>-teaching penetrating the Four Noble Truths (<s>caturāryasatya</s>) that, having heard it, those <s>ṛṣis</s>, splitting with the <s>vajra</s> of knowledge the mountain of the view of the existing personality (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) that had risen up with twenty peaks, realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>śrotaāpattiphala</s>).

body.text: atha te ṛṣayo buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ paricārya saṃprasthitāḥ.
body.translated_text: Then those <s>ṛṣis</s>, having attended upon the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, set forth.

body.text: tena khalu samayena puṇḍravardhane nagare 'ṣṭādaśa dvārāṇy ababhūvan.
body.translated_text: Now at that time there were eighteen gates in the city of <s>Puṇḍravardhana</s>.

body.text: atha bhagavata etad abhavat: yad ahaṃ paścimena dvāreṇa pravekṣyāmi, anyadvāranivāsināṃ nāgarāṇām anyathātvaṃ bhaviṣyati, yan nv aham aṣṭādaśa buddhān abhinirmāya svayaṃ paścimena dvāreṇa praveśayam iti.
body.translated_text: Then this occurred to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'If I enter by the western gate, the townspeople dwelling at the other gates will be disappointed; what if I, having magically created eighteen <s>Buddhas</s>, myself enter by the western gate?'

body.text: atha bhagavān aṣṭādaśa buddhān abhinirmāyā svayaṃ paścimena dvāreṇa praviṣṭaḥ.
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having magically created eighteen <s>Buddhas</s>, himself entered by the western gate.

body.text: bhagavataḥ purapraveśe evaṃrūpāṇy āścaryāṇy atyadbhutāni bhavanty anyāni ca: tadyathonnatonnatāḥ pṛthivīpradeśāḥ avanamanty avanatāś connamanti, apagatapāṣānaśarkarakaṭhalyā bhavanti, nīcāni dvārāṇy uccībhavanti, saṃkṣiptāni viśālībhavanti, hastinaḥ kūjanti, aśvā heṣante, uṣṭrāḥ krośante, gāvo rambhante, vṛṣabhā nandante, mayūrāḥ kekāyante, gṛhagatāni ca vividhāni vādyabhāṇḍāni svayaṃ nadanti, andhāś cakṣūṃsi pratilabhante, badhirāḥ śṛṇvanti, mūkāḥ pravyāhārasamarthā bhavanti, paribhraṣṭendriyavikalā indriyāṇi paripūrnāṇi pratilabhante, madyamadanākṣiptā vimadī bhavanti, viṣapītā nirviṣā bhavanti, anyonyavairiṇo maitrīṃ pratilabhante, garbhiṇyaḥ svastinā prasūyante, bandhanabaddhāḥ pramucyante, adhanā dhanāni pratilabhante.
body.translated_text: At the <s>Bhagavān's</s> entry into the city, marvels of this kind, most wondrous, occurred, and others too: namely, the high places of the ground sank down and the sunken places rose up; they became free of stones, gravel, and pebbles; the low gates became high; the narrow ones became broad; elephants trumpeted, horses neighed, camels bellowed, cows lowed, bulls rejoiced, peacocks cried out, and the various musical instruments in the houses sounded of themselves; the blind regained their eyes, the deaf heard, the mute became able to speak, those deficient through loss of faculties regained their faculties complete, those overcome by the intoxication of wine became free of intoxication, those who had drunk poison became free of poison, mutual enemies obtained loving-kindness, pregnant women were delivered safely, those bound in fetters were released, and the wealthless obtained wealth.

body.text: evaṃvidhayā vibhūtyā praviśya yena sumāgadhāyā niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ.
body.translated_text: Having entered with such majesty, he approached the dwelling of <s>Sumāgadhā</s>.

body.text: atha sumāgadhā svayam eva gośīrṣacandanodakena bhṛṅgāraṃ pūrayitvā bhagavataḥ pādodakam anuprayacchati bhikṣusaṃghasya ca.
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sumāgadhā</s> herself, having filled a pitcher with water [scented] with <s>gośīrṣa</s> sandalwood, offered foot-water to the <s>Bhagavān</s> and to the community of monks.

body.text:
tataḥ sumāgadhā bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatyaivam āha:
dhanyās te paravādivādamathanaṃ paśyanti ye te mukhaṃ
vistīrṇe sadasi sthitasya vacanaṃ śṛṇvanti ye vā mudā /
lābhas tasya mahān bhaviṣyati ca yaḥ pādau tava śrīnidher
mūrdhnā caiva karadvayena vinayāt saṃpīḍya vandiṣyate //
body.translated_text:
Then <s>Sumāgadhā</s>, having fallen at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, spoke thus:
'Blessed are those who behold your face, which crushes the disputations of rival debaters; or who with joy hear the words of you standing in the wide assembly. And great shall be the gain of him who, out of discipline, pressing together your feet — O treasury of glory — with his head and with both hands, shall reverence them.'

body.text: atha bhagavān purastād bhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ, sukhopaviṣṭaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena svahastena saṃtarpayati saṃpravārayati.
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, seated on the seat prepared before the community of monks, knowing that the community of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> was comfortably seated, satisfied and gratified them with his own hand with pure, excellent hard food and soft food.

body.text: atha puṇḍravardhananivāsī janakāyo bhagavantam apaśyaṃs tadgṛhaṃ bhettum ārabdhaḥ. tato bhagavatā tadgṛhaṃ sphaṭikamayam abhinirmitaṃ, yataḥ sarvo mahājanakāya ādarśanagatam iva bhagavantaṃ bhuñjamānaṃ paśyati bhikṣusaṃghaṃ ca.
body.translated_text: Then the crowd of people dwelling in <s>Puṇḍravardhana</s>, not seeing the <s>Bhagavān</s>, began to break down that house. Thereupon the <s>Bhagavān</s> magically made that house of crystal, so that the whole great crowd of people saw the <s>Bhagavān</s> eating, as though set in a mirror, together with the community of monks.

body.text:
āha ca.
sphaṭikamayam abhūt tad eva ramyaṃ maṇikanakākṣaratnabhakticitraṃ /
sthitam iva purato munīndracandraṃ nagarajano 'pi nirīkṣate samagraḥ //
body.translated_text:
And it is said:
'That very [house] became delightful, made of crystal, variegated with inlay of gems, gold, and crystal jewels; and the whole population of the city too gazed upon the moon-like lord of sages (<s>munīndra</s>) standing as if before [them].'

body.text:
prasādāromāñcitasarvagātrāḥ kṛtāñjaliṃ mūrdhni nipātya hastam /
narā namanti sma munīndracandraṃ surā ivendraṃ bhavanodarastham //
body.translated_text: 'Their every limb thrilled with horripilation from faith, casting their folded hands upon their heads, the people bow to the moon-like lord of sages (<s>munīndra</s>), as the gods [bow] to <s>Indra</s> seated within his palace.'

body.text: atha bhagavān kṛtabhaktakṛtyaḥ purastād bhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ.
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having finished the meal-duty, sat upon the seat prepared before the community of monks.

body.text: tataḥ sumāgadhāpramukho 'ntarjanakāyas te ca nāgarās te ca ṛṣayas te ca devāsuragaruḍayakṣagandharvakinnaramahoragā bhagavantaṃ parivāryāvasthitāḥ.
body.translated_text: Then the inner crowd of people headed by <s>Sumāgadhā</s>, and those townsfolk, and those <s>ṛṣis</s>, and those gods, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>, stood surrounding the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: tato bhagavatā teṣāṃ ca tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃpravedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā kaiścic chrotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣāt kṛtaṃ, kaiścit sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ, kaiścid anāgāmiphalam, kaiścit pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhattvaṃ sākṣāt kṛtaṃ, kaiścid ūṣmagatāni kuśalamūlāni utpāditāni, kaiścin mūrdhānaḥ, kaiścin mṛdumadhyādhimātrakṣāntayaḥ, kaiścic chrāvakabodhau cittāny utpāditāni, kaiścit pratyekāyāṃ bodhau, kaiścid anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, kaiścic charaṇagamanāni gṛhītāni, kaiścic chikṣāpadāni gṛhītāni.
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave them such a <s>Dharma</s>-teaching penetrating the Four Noble Truths (<s>caturāryasatya</s>) that, having heard it, some realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>śrotaāpattiphala</s>), some the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>), some the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>), some, having gone forth [into the homeless life], realized <s>arhattva</s> (arhatship) through the abandonment of all defilements, some produced the wholesome roots [at the stage] of the 'heat' (<s>ūṣmagata</s>), some [those] of the 'summits' (<s>mūrdhan</s>), some the 'forbearances' (<s>kṣānti</s>) of weak, middling, and superior [degree], some produced minds [set] upon the awakening of the <s>śrāvakas</s> (<s>śrāvakabodhi</s>), some upon the awakening of the <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (<s>pratyekabodhi</s>), some upon unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), some took the goings-for-refuge (<s>śaraṇagamana</s>), some took the training-precepts (<s>śikṣāpada</s>).

body.text: yad bhūyasā sā parṣad buddhanimnā dharmapravaṇā saṃghaprāgbhārā vyavasthitā.
body.translated_text: So that for the most part that assembly stood inclined toward the <s>Buddha</s>, bent toward the <s>Dharma</s>, and leaning toward the <s>Saṃgha</s>.

body.text: yadā bhagavataitat sūtraṃ bhāṣitaṃ, tadā bhikṣavo bhagavantam evam āhuḥ: āścaryaṃ bhagavann, āścaryaṃ sugata, yat sumāgadhayā bhagavantaṃ kalyāṇamitram āgamya buddhakāryaṃ kṛtam iti.
body.translated_text: When this <s>sūtra</s> had been spoken by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, then the monks spoke thus to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'It is a marvel, O <s>Bhagavān</s>! It is a marvel, O <s>Sugata</s>, that <s>Sumāgadhā</s>, having resorted to the <s>Bhagavān</s> as a spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), accomplished the Buddha-task (<s>buddhakārya</s>)!'

body.text: bhagavān āha: na bhikṣava etarhy eva yathātīte 'py adhvani buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ kalyāṇamitram āgamya kāñcanamālayā yad buddhakāryaṃ kṛtaṃ, tac chṛṇuta, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kurute, bhāṣiṣye.
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Not only now, O monks, but in a past age as well, <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>, having resorted to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, as a spiritual friend, accomplished the Buddha-task — hear that, and attend to it well and thoroughly; I shall speak.'

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ, bhikṣavo, 'tīte 'dhvani viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma śāstā loka udapādi, tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān, sa bārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati ṛṣivadane mṛgadāve.
body.translated_text: Formerly, O monks, in a past age, when [people's] lifespan among the population was twenty thousand years, a teacher named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed charioteer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and men, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. Depending upon the city of <s>Bārāṇasī</s>, he dwelt in the <s>Ṛṣivadana</s> deer park (<s>mṛgadāva</s>).

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena kṛkī nāma rājā babhūva.
body.translated_text: Now at that time there was a king named <s>Kṛkin</s>.

body.text: tasya duhitā kāñcanamālayā śirasi baddhayā jātā, tasyā mātāpitṛbhyāṃ kāñcanamāleti nāma kṛtam.
body.translated_text: A daughter was born to him with [a tuft of hair] bound upon her head like a garland of gold; her mother and father gave her the name <s>Kāñcanamālā</s> ('Golden Garland').

body.text: sā unnītā vardhitā mahatī saṃvṛttā, rājñaḥ kṛkina iṣṭā kāntā priyā manāpā saṃvṛttā.
body.translated_text: She was raised and brought up and became grown; she became wished-for, beloved, dear, and pleasing to King <s>Kṛkin</s>.

body.text: sā pañcaśataparivārā bhagavato darśanāyopasaṃkrāntā, tasyā bhagavatā dharmo deśitaḥ.
body.translated_text: She, with a retinue of five hundred, approached to see the <s>Bhagavān</s>; the <s>Dharma</s> was taught to her by the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: tayā taṃ dharmaṃ śrutvā bhagavato 'nitike mahān cittaprasāda utpanno, bhagavāṃś ca tayā yāvajjīvaṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātraśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraḥ pracāritah.
body.translated_text: Having heard that <s>Dharma</s>, a great clarity of mind (<s>cittaprasāda</s>) toward the <s>Bhagavān</s> arose in her, and she provided the <s>Bhagavān</s>, for as long as he lived, with robes, alms-food, bowl, bedding and seat, and medicines and requisites for illness.

body.text:
tena khalu punaḥ samayena rājñā kṛkinā daśa svapnā dṛṣṭāḥ:
(1) vātāyanena hastī nirgatas, puccho lagnaḥ.
(2) tṛṣitaya pṛṣṭhataḥ kūpo dhāvati.
(3) muktāprasthaṃ śaktuprasthena vikrīyamāṇaṃ.
(4) candanaṃ kāṣṭhārgheṇa samīkriyamāṇaṃ.
(5) gandhahastinaṃ kalabhair vitrāsyamānaṃ.
(6) āramaṃ puṣpaphalasaṃpannam adattadāyibhir apahriyamāṇam.
(7) aśucinā mrakṣito markaṭaḥ parān upaliṃpyamānaḥ.
(8) markaṭasya rājyābhiṣekaḥ.
(9) paṭo 'ṣṭādaśabhir janair ākṛṣyate, na śīryate.
(10) mahājanakāyaś caikatra saṃnipatya kalahabhaṇḍanavigrahavivāde nātināmayati.
body.translated_text: Now at that time, King <s>Kṛkin</s> had ten dreams: (1) An elephant exited through a window, but its tail got stuck. (2) A well ran after a thirsty person from behind. (3) A measure of pearls being sold for a measure of barley flour. (4) Sandalwood being valued at the price of ordinary wood. (5) A rutting elephant being frightened by young calves. (6) A garden rich in flowers and fruits being plundered by thieves. (7) A monkey smeared with filth, smearing others. (8) The royal consecration of a monkey. (9) A cloth being pulled by eighteen people, yet it does not tear. (10) A great crowd of people gathering in one place and not settling their quarrels, disputes, and conflicts.

body.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punar bhītaś trastaś cintayati: mā me itonidānaṃ rājyāc cyutir bhaviṣyati jīvitasya cāntarāya iti.
body.translated_text: Having seen these, he became frightened and alarmed, thinking: 'May there not be, on account of these, a fall from my kingdom or a threat to my life.'

body.text: tato rājñā svapnādhyāyavido brāhmaṇān āhūya svapnān niveditavān.
body.translated_text: Then the king summoned <s>brāhmaṇas</s> skilled in the interpretation of dreams and reported the dreams to them.

body.text: te kāñcanamālāṃ dṛṣṭvā kathayanti: rājan, yā te sarvajanapriyā tasyā rudhireṇa yajño yaṣṭavyaḥ, antrair nagaraṃ veṣṭavyam, evaṃ devasya śreyo bhaviṣyati, svapnān dāruṇān dṛṣṭvā rājyajīvitahāriṇo 'nenopāyena svastir devasya bhaviṣyati.
body.translated_text: They, seeing <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>, said: 'O King, with the blood of her who is beloved by all people, a sacrifice must be performed, and the city must be encircled with her entrails. Thus will there be welfare for Your Majesty. Having seen terrible dreams that threaten the kingdom and life, by this means there will be safety for Your Majesty.'

body.text: rājā saṃlakṣayati: sarvajanapriyā me kāñcanamālā, tāṃ vyāpādayitukāmā brāhmaṇā evam āhuḥ. varaṃ mamaiva maraṇaṃ, na tu kāñcanamālāṃ vyāpādayiṣyāmīti.
body.translated_text: The king reflected: '<s>Kāñcanamālā</s>, who is beloved by all people, is mine. The <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, wishing to destroy her, say this. Better that I myself should die, but I shall not cause <s>Kāñcanamālā</s> to be killed.'

body.text: kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ, kāñcanamālayā dṛṣṭaḥ. sā kathayati: kim evaṃ cintāparo, deva, iti. tena sa vṛttānto vistareṇa niveditaḥ. sā kathayati: eṣa bhagavān kāśyapaḥ samyaksaṃbuddho bārāṇasīm upaniśritya viharati ṛṣivadane mṛgadāve, taṃ bhagavantaṃ gatvā pṛcchatha. yathā te bhagavān vyākaroti tathaivaṃ dhāraya.
body.translated_text: Placing his cheek in his hand, he sat absorbed in anxiety. He was seen by <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>. She said: 'Why are you so anxious, Your Majesty?' He reported the whole matter to her in detail. She said: 'There is the <s>Bhagavān Kāśyapa</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One, dwelling near <s>Bārāṇasī</s> at the Deer Park in <s>Ṛṣivadana</s>. Go and ask that <s>Bhagavān</s>. As the <s>Bhagavān</s> explains it, so you should understand it.'

body.text: tato rājā mahatā śrīsamudāyena kāñcanamālayā sārdhaṃ barāṇasyā nirgatya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ, upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ, kāñcanamālāpi, anyāni ca brāhmaṇagṛhapatiśatasahasrāṇi.
body.translated_text: Then the king, with great royal splendor, together with <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>, departed from <s>Bārāṇasī</s> and approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> feet and sat to one side — as did <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>, and also other hundreds of thousands of <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders.

body.text: atha bhagavān kṛkinaṃ rājānaṃ dharmayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati. anekaparyāyeṇa dharmayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīṃ babhūva.
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> instructed, encouraged, inspired, and delighted King <s>Kṛkin</s> with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>. Having in many ways instructed, encouraged, inspired, and delighted him with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent.

body.text: atha kṛkī rājā daśa svapnān nivedyaivam āha: mā me, bhagavaṃs, tatonidānaṃ rājyāc cyutir bhaviṣyati jīvitasya cāntarāya iti.
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Kṛkin</s>, having reported the ten dreams, spoke thus: 'May there not be, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, on account of these, a fall from my kingdom or a threat to my life.'

body.text:
bhagavān āha: mā bhaiṣīs tvaṃ, mahāraja, na tavetonidānaṃ rājyāc cyutir bhaviṣyatīti jīvitasya cāntarāyaḥ.
(1) yat tvaṃ, mahārāja, svapnam adrākṣīr, vātāyanena hastī nirgacchan puccho lagna iti, bhaviṣyaty anāgate 'dhvani varṣaśatāyuṣi prajāyāṃ śākyamunir nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ, sa sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kṛtvendhanakṣayād ivāgnir anupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāsyatīti. tasya parinirvṛtasya paścime kāle aśrāddhā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayas, te rudanto 'śrumukhān bandhūn utsṛjya pravrajya vihāreṣu gṛhasaṃjñām utpādayiṣyanti, tasyaitat pūrvanimittam.
(2) yat tvaṃ punaḥ svapnam adrākṣīs, tṛṣitasya pṛṣṭhataḥ kūpo dhāvati, tasyaiva śravakā dharmaṃ deśayiṣyanti śraddhānāṃ gṛhapatīnāṃ, te satṛṣṇā eva prakramiṣyanti, tasyaitat pūrvanimittam.
(3) yat tvaṃ svapnam adrākṣīr, muktāprasthena śaktuprasthaṃ krīyamāṇam iti, tasyaiva śrāvakāḥ śaktuprasthasya hetor indriyabalabodhyaṅgāni saṃprakāśayiṣyanti, tasyaitat pūrvanimittam.
(4) yat tvaṃ svapnam adrākṣīś, candanaṃ kāṣṭhārgheṇa samīkriyamāṇaṃ, tasyaiva śrāvakās taṃ tīrthikavākyam anugṛhya saddharmeṇa samīkariṣyanti, tasyaitat pūrvanimittam.
(5) yat tvaṃ svapnam adrākṣīr, gandhahastī kalabhair vitrāsyata iti, tasyaiva śrāvakā asaṃyatās te śīlavanto bhikṣūn niṣkāśayiṣyanti, tasyaitat pūrvanimittam.
(6) yat tvaṃ svapnam adrākṣīr, ārāmāṃ puṣpaphalasaṃpannaṃ adattādāyibhir apahriyamāṇaṃ, tasyaiva śrāvakā āryasaṃghasya pratipāditam ārāmaṃ saṃgham ālaṃbīkṛtya kecid abhāvitakāyā abhāvitacittā abhāvitaprajñāḥ saṃghād ācchidya puṣpaphalaṃ svajanebhyo dāsyanti, tasyaitat pūrvanimittam.
(7) yat tvaṃ svapnam adrākṣīr, aśucimrakṣito markaṭaḥ parān upaliṃpyatīti, tasyaiva śrāvakā abhāvitakāyā abhāvitacittā abhāvitaprajñā ātmanāpattim āpannāḥ śrāddhānām api bhikṣūṇām āpattiṃ vyavasthāpayiṣyanti, tasyaitat pūrvanimittam.
(8) yat tvaṃ svapnam adrākṣīr, markaṭasya rājyābhiṣekaḥ, tasmin samaye vikalendriyā api rājāno bhaviṣyanti, tasyaitat pūrvanimittam.
(9) yat tvaṃ svapnam adrākṣīḥ, paṭo 'ṣṭādaśabhir janair ākṛṣyate na ca śīryata iti, tasya parinirvṛtasya śāsanam aṣṭādaśabhedabhinnaṃ bhaviṣyati, na ca śakyati vimuktipaṭaṃ pāṭayituṃ, tasyaitat pūrvanimittam.
(10) yat tvaṃ svapnam adrākṣīr, mahājanakāyaś caikatra saṃnipatya kalahabhaṇḍena vivādavigrahenātināmayanti, tasya śāsane asaṃyatā bhikṣavaḥ kalahabhaṇḍanavigrahavivādenāntardhāpayiṣyanti, tasyaitat pūrvanimittam.
mā bhaiṣīs tvaṃ, mahārāja, na tavetonidānaṃ rājyāc cyutir bhaviṣyati jīvitāntarāyo vā.
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Fear not, Great King. There will not be, on account of these, a fall from your kingdom or a threat to your life. (1) The dream you saw, Great King, of an elephant exiting through a window with its tail stuck — in the future time, when the lifespan of people is a hundred years, there will arise a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One. Having accomplished the entire work of a <s>Buddha</s>, he will pass into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>nirvāṇa</s> realm without remainder, like a fire whose fuel is exhausted. After his passing, in the final period, faithless <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders will abandon their weeping, tear-faced relatives, go forth as renunciants, and in the monasteries generate the perception of a household — this is the portent of that. (2) The dream you saw of a well running after a thirsty person from behind — his disciples will teach the <s>Dharma</s> to faithful householders, but they will depart still full of craving — this is the portent of that. (3) The dream you saw of a measure of pearls being purchased for a measure of barley flour — his disciples will, for the sake of a measure of barley flour, proclaim the faculties, powers, and factors of awakening — this is the portent of that. (4) The dream you saw of sandalwood being valued at the price of ordinary wood — his disciples will adopt the words of non-Buddhist teachers and equate them with the true <s>Dharma</s> — this is the portent of that. (5) The dream you saw of a rutting elephant being frightened by young calves — his undisciplined disciples will expel virtuous <s>bhikṣus</s> — this is the portent of that. (6) The dream you saw of a garden rich in flowers and fruits being plundered by thieves — his disciples, some undeveloped in body, undeveloped in mind, undeveloped in wisdom, will seize gardens given to the noble <s>Saṅgha</s>, and using the <s>Saṅgha</s> as a pretext, will give the flowers and fruits to their own relatives — this is the portent of that. (7) The dream you saw of a monkey smeared with filth smearing others — his disciples, undeveloped in body, mind, and wisdom, having themselves fallen into offenses, will attribute offenses to faithful <s>bhikṣus</s> as well — this is the portent of that. (8) The dream you saw of the royal consecration of a monkey — at that time, even those with deficient faculties will become kings — this is the portent of that. (9) The dream you saw of a cloth being pulled by eighteen people but not tearing — his teaching will be divided into eighteen sects, yet the cloth of liberation cannot be torn — this is the portent of that. (10) The dream you saw of a great crowd of people gathering in one place and not settling their quarrels, disputes, and conflicts — undisciplined <s>bhikṣus</s> in his teaching will cause the teaching to disappear through quarrels, disputes, and conflicts — this is the portent of that. Fear not, Great King. There will not be, on account of these, a fall from your kingdom, nor a threat to your life.'

body.text: tato bhagavatā tasya rājñas tasya ca mahājanakāyasya tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā caturaśītyā prāṇiśatasahasraiḥ satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam.
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave to that king and to that great assembly such a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> that penetrates the Four Noble Truths, that upon hearing it, eighty-four hundred thousand beings gained the vision of truth.

body.text: kāñcanamālayā bhagavantaṃ kalyāṇamitram āgamya buddhakāryaṃ kṛtam.
body.translated_text: For <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>, having gained the <s>Bhagavān</s> as her spiritual friend, the work of a <s>Buddha</s> was accomplished.

body.text: kiṃ manyadhve, bhikṣavaḥ yāsau kāñcanamālā iyam eva sā sumāgadheti.
body.translated_text: What do you think, <s>bhikṣus</s>? She who was <s>Kāñcanamālā</s> — she is none other than this <s>Sumāgadhā</s>.

body.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kiṃ bhadanta, kāñcanamālayā karma kṛtaṃ yenāḍhye kule pratyajātā yena kāñcanamālayā śirasi baddhayā jātā iti.
body.translated_text: The <s>bhikṣus</s>, filled with doubt, asked the <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'Venerable sir, what <s>karma</s> did <s>Kāñcanamālā</s> perform that she was reborn in a wealthy family, born with a golden garland on her head?'

body.text: bhagavān āha: kāñcanamālayaiva, bhikṣavaḥ, pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāny oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni. kāñcanamālayaiva, bhikṣavaḥ, karmāṇi kṛtāni upacitāni. ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati. na, bhikṣavaḥ, karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhyapṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātāv, api tūpātteṣu eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca.
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: '<s>Bhikṣus</s>, it was <s>Kāñcanamālā</s> herself who, in previous births, performed and accumulated <s>karmas</s>, whose provisions were complete, whose conditions had matured, which stood ready like a flood, and which were inevitable. <s>Bhikṣus</s>, it was <s>Kāñcanamālā</s> herself who performed and accumulated the <s>karmas</s>. Who else would experience their results? <s>Bhikṣus</s>, <s>karmas</s> performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, <s>karmas</s> performed ripen only in the appropriated <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases), whether wholesome or unwholesome.'

body.text:
na pranaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api /
sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām //
body.translated_text: <s>Karmas</s> do not perish even after hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> (ten millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons); having obtained the right conditions and the right time, they certainly bear fruit for embodied beings.

body.text: bhūtapūrvam, bhikṣavo, 'tīte 'dhvani bārāṇasyāṃ mahānagaryām anyatamā daridrā strī, tayā pratyekabuddhasya caitye nānāvicitrāṃ palālamālāṃ granthayitvā samāropya prasannacittayā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam.
body.translated_text: <s>Bhikṣus</s>, in the past, in a former time, in the great city of <s>Bārāṇasī</s>, there lived a certain poor woman. She wove a garland of various colorful straw and placed it upon the <s>caitya</s> (shrine) of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, and with a serene mind she made a vow.

body.text: anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca yatrayatropapadye 'haṃ tatratatra kāñcanamālayā śirasi baddhayā jāyeyam iti. kiṃ manyadhve, bhikṣavaḥ. yāsau daridrā strī, iyam asau kāñcanamālā. yad anayā prasannacittayā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ, tena pañcajanmaśatāni kāñcanamālayā śirasi baddhayā jātā.
body.translated_text: 'By this root of merit, by this arising of intention, and by this gift of giving, wherever I am reborn, may I always be born with a golden garland on my head.' What do you think, <s>bhikṣus</s>? She who was that poor woman — she is this <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>. Because she made that vow with a serene mind, for five hundred lifetimes she has been born with a golden garland on her head.

body.text: paṇadvayaṃ ca tayā paṭāntāvabaddhaṃ vimucyāryasaṃghāya dattaṃ; tenāḍhyesu kulesu jātā praṇidhānavaśāc ceti.
body.translated_text: And she untied two <s>paṇas</s> (coins) that had been tied in the hem of her garment and gave them to the noble <s>Saṅgha</s>; through that [merit], she was born in wealthy families, and by the power of her aspiration.

body.text: atha bhagavān sumāgadhāpramukhaṃ puṇḍravardhananivāsinaṃ mahājanakāyam abhiprasādya prakrāntaḥ, tathaiva rddhyā sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena śrāvastīm āgataḥ.
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), having inspired faith in the great assembly of people dwelling in <s>Puṇḍravardhana</s>, led by <s>Sumāgadhā</s>, departed. In the same manner, by supernatural power, together with the community of monks, he came to <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

body.text: iti hi, bhikṣava, ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklo, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ. tasmāt tarhi, bhikṣava, ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīya iti. tasmāt tarhi, bhikṣava, evaṃ śikṣitavyam, yac chāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāma ity evaṃ vo, bhikṣavaḥ, śikṣitavyam.
body.translated_text: Thus, monks, the ripening of exclusively dark deeds is exclusively dark; the ripening of exclusively bright deeds is exclusively bright; and that of mixed deeds is mixed. Therefore, monks, having abandoned exclusively dark deeds and mixed deeds, you should direct your efforts solely toward exclusively bright deeds. Therefore, monks, you should train thus: 'We shall honor the Teacher, we shall revere him, we shall respect him, we shall worship him.' Thus, monks, should you train.

body.text: idam avocad bhagavān āttamanās, te ca bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandann iti. sumāgadhāvadānaṃ samāptam.
body.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> words. The <s>Sumāgadhāvadāna</s> is concluded.
